# Data Dictionaries 5: Crosswalks Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Let a Data Sources editor map many datasets with different column layouts (`zip_code`, `zip`, `postal_code`) onto one reference layout, one layout family at a time, and save the result as a **combined dataset**: a virtual dataset that stacks every mapped dataset, with codes reconciled through dictionary code lists, a `source_dataset` column, a mapping that exports as CSV, and a banner when a code list it decoded with has changed.

**Architecture:** Five new tables (`crosswalks`, `crosswalks__layouts`, `crosswalks__columns`, `crosswalks__datasets`, `crosswalks__mappings`) hold the crosswalk. Signed-in users read them under Data Sources RLS and write the children only through `rpc_crosswalks__save`, which replaces one crosswalk's columns, layouts, memberships, and mappings in one transaction. All matching, layout grouping, and SQL compilation are pure TypeScript in `shared/models/crosswalks/`, reusing slice 2's scorer (`ColumnProfile.getMatchScore`), slice 3's coding fit (`DictionaryMatch`), and slice 4's `ColumnConversion` `CASE` renderer for code translation. The browser compiles a `SELECT ... UNION ALL BY NAME ...` over every mapped dataset and saves it through `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset`, which creates or updates the combined virtual dataset, reconciles its columns by name, writes reference bindings for its coded columns (so the code-list tag, Ask Avandar, and Used by work with no new agent code), and records a fingerprint of every code list it embedded.

**Tech Stack:** Supabase Postgres (declarative schemas, pgTAP), TypeScript, React 19, Mantine 9 (`Stepper`, `Table`, `SegmentedControl`, `Select`, `Modal`, `Tooltip`, `Progress`), TanStack Query and Router, zod 4, Lingui, DuckDB-WASM 1.33.1-dev20.0 (DuckDB v1.4.4) through QETL, `@duckdb/node-api` 1.5.5 for executed tests, papaparse 5 for the mapping CSV, `@tanstack/react-virtual` 3 (Part B), Vitest, Playwright.

**Spec:** [data-dictionaries-design.md](data-dictionaries-design.md), slice 5 of section 16. Read sections 3, 4, 5.4, 5.5, 7.1, 7.2, 7.6, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, and 18 first. The Refinements at the end of this file override the spec where they differ; the spec edits this plan makes, and the owner decisions it needs, are listed there too.

**Scope:** Slice 5: the crosswalk schema and RLS, layouts and their signatures, the three steps (Choose datasets, Map each dataset, Create combined dataset), mapping fills and conversions, compilation, the combined dataset, **Export mapping**, the stale banner, the Crosswalks list group and **New crosswalk**, Used by's **Crosswalk** rows, AI meaning suggestions for mappings, a virtualized layout list past 100 layouts, per-dataset progress while combining, and the measurement open decision 4 asks for. Out: side-by-side joins, write-back to live sources, "Add from datasets into an existing dictionary", and everything else in spec section 17.

**Delivery:** two parts, each a mergeable PR (recommended owner decision 1). **Part A** (Tasks 0 to 28, feature F136) ships the schema, the engine, every surface in spec section 7.6, export, the stale banner, and Used by. **Part B** (Tasks 29 to 33, feature F137) is frontend only: meaning suggestions, the long layout list, combining progress, and the 100-dataset measurement. Part A's migration carries everything Part B needs.

**Builds on:** slice 1 ([plan](data-dictionaries-1-dictionaries-plan.md), F129) for the dictionary tables and their RLS conventions; slice 2 ([plan](data-dictionaries-2-inference-plan.md), F130) for `profileDatasetColumns`, `ColumnProfile` (the scorer and name helpers), `DictionarySuggestions`, `PickDatasetsTable`, `NewDictionaryFooter`, and `useListPaneToggle`; slice 3 ([plan](data-dictionaries-3-attach-plan.md), F131) and F132 for bindings, `DictionaryMatch`, `ColumnCodes`, the code-list popover, the rail group, and Used by; slice 4 ([plan](data-dictionaries-4-conversions-plan.md), F133, F134) for `ColumnConversion`, the `ava_raw_<datasetId>` view, linked datasets, the virtual dataset definition token, and `clearCachedDatasetRows`.

**Prototype:** none. The prototype the spec names is gone. Spec section 7.6 is the only description of the crosswalk surfaces. They are new surfaces, designed with the `impeccable` skill in Tasks 17 and 19 to 23.

House conventions (unchanged from slice 4):

- `shared/` imports siblings with `.ts` and never imports `src/`. `src/` imports shared through `$/` without the extension.
- Import a model's entry file and use its namespace (`CrosswalkMapping.Fill`, `CrosswalkLayout.Status`). Files inside a model folder may import sibling `*.types.ts` files.
- Every user-facing string goes through Lingui (`<Trans>`, `<Plural>`, `plural`, or `t` from `useLingui()`). Placeholders are named variables (`${datasetName}`), never expressions. Compute a plural into its own variable and never put `plural()` inside `t`. Numbers shown to the user go through `i18n.number`. Never pass `t` into a module-level helper: modules return structured data and the component translates it. No em dashes anywhere, including comments.
- Functions stay at 45 lines or fewer. Docstrings on every exported function, type, constant, and module key, saying what it is for. Comments describe the code as it is, never this plan, its parts, or its slices.
- A name or label is data, never SQL: every literal goes through `quoteSqlLiteral` and every identifier through `quoteSqlIdentifier` (both from `@avandar/utils/sql`).
- jsonb written by this plan never uses ids as object keys: the parsers run `camelCaseKeysDeep`, which would rewrite a uuid key. Maps keyed by id are stored as arrays of objects (`[{ "code_list_id": ..., "fingerprint": ... }]`).
- Component tests use `render`, `renderHook`, `screen`, `fireEvent`, `waitFor`, `within`, `act`, and `TestProviders` from `@/test-utils`. A hook that calls `useLingui` renders with `{ wrapper: TestProviders }`. Mantine `Select` options: `queryAllByRole("option", { hidden: true })`.
- Run one Vitest file: `pnpm vitest run <path>`. Run one executed test: `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.executed.config.ts <path>`.
- Before each commit format what you touched: `pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path .oxfmtignore <ts/tsx files>`, `pnpm exec eslint --fix <files>`, `pnpm exec stylelint <css files>`, and `pnpm exec prettier --write <sql files>`.
- Verify types with `pnpm exec tsc -b --force --noEmit` (plain `tsc -b` can report clean from a stale cache) and the edge functions with `pnpm type-check:deno`.
- Commit by explicit path, never `git add -A`. End each commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- The pre-push hook adds machine translations and formats files, so a push leaves changes in the tree; that is expected.
- Run `pnpm test:db` on its own, never in parallel with the frontend suite. `test:frontend` has one known failure, `src/routes/_auth/$workspaceSlug/dashboards/edit/-$dashboardId.test.tsx` (maplibre `createObjectURL`), which is not this plan's to fix.

Task 11 runs a dataset named `Kings O'Brien $& --` and a label with `'` through real DuckDB |
| Privacy and security on the server | Both RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER with `search_path = ''`, check Data Sources editor before reading anything else, raise one error for a missing and a forbidden id, refuse ids from another crosswalk or workspace, and never remove a membership the caller cannot read (Tasks 3, 4). `output_dataset_id`, `compiled_at`, and `compiled_code_lists` are managed columns a signed-in user cannot set (Task 1) |

## Decisions settled while planning

### The stacked SQL on both DuckDB builds

A scratch script ran the same statements on `@duckdb/node-api` 1.5.5 (DuckDB v1.5.5) and on the browser's DuckDB-WASM build loaded through `duckdb-node-blocking.cjs` (`SELECT version()` returns `v1.4.4`). Both agree on every row.

| Probe | Result | What the compiler does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SELECT * FROM t1 UNION ALL BY NAME SELECT * FROM t2` with `CaseNo`/`caseno` and `GENDER` (`INTEGER`) / `gender` (`VARCHAR`) | One column per name, matched ignoring case, named as in the first branch; mixed types become `VARCHAR` | Datasets of one layout share their names ignoring case, so a layout's datasets stack with `SELECT *` |
| A branch whose expressions have no `AS` alias | `UNION ALL BY NAME` makes a new column per unaliased expression (`CAST(__ava_source_dataset AS VARCHAR)`) and fills the others with `NULL` | Every output expression in every branch is aliased |
| `"caseno"` against a column named `CaseNo` | Resolves: quoted identifiers match ignoring case | A fill's `sourceColumn` resolves in every dataset of its layout |
| `lpad('123456', 5, '0')` | `12345`: `lpad` truncates | `pad_text` pads only a digit string shorter than the length and never truncates |
| `strptime('13/45/2026', '%m/%d/%Y')` | `Invalid Input Error`: one bad value fails the whole query | Dates parse with `TRY_STRPTIME`, which returns `NULL` |
| `TRY_CAST(1.5::DOUBLE AS BIGINT)`, `TRY_CAST('x' AS BIGINT)` | `2`, `NULL` | Every fill is cast to its column's type with `TRY_CAST`; the pane's example shows what becomes empty |
| `CAST(501.0::DOUBLE AS VARCHAR)` | `501.0` | `pad_text` is offered only for whole-number and text sources |
| `regexp_full_match('00501', '[0-9]+')`, `regexp_replace(trim('  New   York  '), '\s+', ' ', 'g')` | `true`, `New York` | Used by `pad_text` and `trim_and_fix_case` |
| The full stacked statement (two layouts, a nested per-layout `UNION ALL BY NAME`, a decode `CASE`, `TRY_STRPTIME`, typed `NULL`s) | Six rows, columns `source_dataset VARCHAR, case_id VARCHAR, sex VARCHAR, rash_onset_date DATE` | The shape in "Contracts" below |

### The SQL analyzer reads every stacked dataset

`DuckDbSqlAnalyzer.getReadDatasetIdsFromSql` was run through Vitest on the compiled shape (two layouts, a nested `UNION ALL BY NAME` per layout, a dataset name with `''`), and on the same SQL wrapped as `SELECT * FROM (...) LIMIT 20` and `SELECT count(*) AS "rows" FROM (...)`. It returned all three dataset ids each time, so `WorkspaceQuerySession.runQuery` admits and loads every source, and a combined dataset's dependency staleness covers every source.

### Two more findings

- **Code-list `updated_at` cannot detect a changed list.** `data_dictionaries__write_code_lists` upserts every list of a dictionary on every save with no `is distinct from` guard, so `updated_at` moves on every save, changed or not. Spec 5.4's `compiled_code_list_versions` (id to `updated_at`) would show the stale banner after any edit to the dictionary. The crosswalk stores a fingerprint of each embedded list's pairs instead (`compiled_code_lists`), compared in the browser.
- **No RPC updates a virtual dataset's SQL and columns.** Data Explorer's "Save over" updates `raw_sql` only and leaves `dataset_columns` stale, and the loaded view in DuckDB is not keyed by the SQL. The combined-dataset RPC reconciles columns by name (keeping ids, so bindings and descriptions survive), and the browser clears the dataset's cached rows and the virtual dataset query cache after it (Tasks 4, 23).

## Contracts

Every task builds against these names. A task that needs one defined in another task imports it; nothing here is renamed later. Hints are stable strings the client maps to copy.

### Schema (Tasks 1 to 5)

Enums, one file each (`supabase/schemas/00.enum.<name>.sql`):

| Type | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `crosswalks__codes_output` | `labels`, `codes` |
| `crosswalks__layout_status` | `to_do`, `review`, `mapped`, `skipped` |
| `crosswalks__mapping_status` | `suggested`, `confirmed` |
| `crosswalks__mapping_reason` | `name_and_type`, `same_values`, `similar_layout`, `meaning` |

`public.crosswalks` (`11.crosswalks.sql`: it references `datasets`, which `10.datasets.sql` creates), shaped like `data_dictionaries`:

| Column | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid()` | |
| `workspace_id` | `uuid not null` | `references workspaces on update cascade on delete cascade` |
| `owner_id` | `uuid not null default auth.uid()` | `references auth.users on delete no action` |
| `owner_profile_id` | `uuid not null` | `references user_profiles on delete no action`; validated against owner and workspace by trigger |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | `timestamptz not null default now()` | `util__set_updated_at` |
| `name` | `text not null` | `check (btrim(name) <> '')` |
| `description` | `text` | |
| `output_dataset_id` | `uuid` | `references datasets (id) on update cascade on delete set null`. Managed |
| `codes_output_as` | `crosswalks__codes_output not null default 'labels'` | |
| `adds_source_column` | `boolean not null default true` | |
| `compiled_at` | `timestamptz` | Managed |
| `compiled_code_lists` | `jsonb` | Managed. `[{ "code_list_id": uuid, "fingerprint": text }]`, the lists the combined dataset embedded |

`unique (id, workspace_id)`. Triggers: `crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change`, `crosswalks__guard_managed_columns` (a signed-in user may not insert or change `owner_id`, `owner_profile_id`, `output_dataset_id`, `compiled_at`, `compiled_code_lists`; inserts must leave the last three null; RI actions and SECURITY DEFINER functions run as another role and pass, exactly like `datasets__virtual__guard_linked_source`), `crosswalks__validate_owner_profile`, `set_updated_at`. Indexes on `(workspace_id, owner_id)`, `owner_profile_id`, and a partial index on `output_dataset_id where output_dataset_id is not null`. Policies copy `data_dictionaries` word for word with "crosswalks": select for Data Sources viewers, insert for editors who own the row, update for editors (`with check`), delete for the owner who is an editor or any Data Sources admin.

Children (`workspace_id uuid not null`, `crosswalk_id uuid not null`, composite `foreign key (crosswalk_id, workspace_id) references crosswalks (id, workspace_id) on update cascade on delete cascade`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` with its trigger except on `crosswalks__datasets`). Signed-in users get `select` only; `service_role` gets select, insert, update, delete; the only write path is `rpc_crosswalks__save`.

| Table (file) | Columns | Constraints |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crosswalks__layouts` (`20.crosswalks__layouts.sql`) | `id uuid pk`, `signature text not null`, `column_names text[] not null`, `is_reference boolean not null default false`, `status crosswalks__layout_status not null default 'to_do'` | `unique (crosswalk_id, signature)`, `unique (id, crosswalk_id)`, unique index `(crosswalk_id) where is_reference`, `check (not is_reference or status = 'mapped')`, `check (cardinality(column_names) > 0)` |
| `crosswalks__columns` (`21.crosswalks__columns.sql`: it references `data_dictionaries__entries`, which sorts after `20.crosswalks__*`) | `id uuid pk`, `name text not null`, `position integer not null`, `data_type datasets__ava_data_type not null`, `entry_id uuid references data_dictionaries__entries (id) on update cascade on delete set null` | `check (btrim(name) <> '')`, `check (name = btrim(name))`, unique index `(crosswalk_id, lower(name))` (no `btrim` in the index: the desktop's SQLite twin has no `btrim`), `unique (id, crosswalk_id)`, index on `entry_id` |
| `crosswalks__datasets` (`21.crosswalks__datasets.sql`) | `id uuid pk`, `dataset_id uuid not null`, `layout_id uuid not null` | `foreign key (dataset_id) references datasets (id) on update cascade on delete cascade`, `foreign key (layout_id, crosswalk_id) references crosswalks__layouts (id, crosswalk_id) on update cascade on delete cascade`, `unique (crosswalk_id, dataset_id)`, index on `dataset_id` |
| `crosswalks__mappings` (`22.crosswalks__mappings.sql`) | `id uuid pk`, `layout_id uuid not null`, `column_id uuid not null`, `fill jsonb not null`, `status crosswalks__mapping_status not null default 'suggested'`, `confidence numeric`, `reason crosswalks__mapping_reason` | composite foreign keys to layouts and columns `(…, crosswalk_id)` with cascade, `unique (layout_id, column_id)`, `check (confidence is null or confidence between 0 and 1)`, `check (jsonb_typeof(fill) = 'object')` |

Select policies: Data Sources viewer on the row's workspace for every child; `crosswalks__datasets` also requires `util__auth_user_can_access_resource('dataset', dataset_id, 'viewer')`, so a reader never learns about a dataset they cannot open.

RPCs (both SECURITY DEFINER, `search_path = ''`, `authenticated` only, revoke-then-grant):

```sql
-- Replaces one crosswalk's settings, columns, layouts, memberships, and
-- mappings with the given sets in one transaction.
-- p_settings: { name, description, codes_output_as, adds_source_column }
-- p_columns:  [{ id, name, position, data_type, entry_id }]
-- p_layouts:  [{ id, signature, column_names, is_reference, status }]
-- p_datasets: [{ dataset_id, layout_id }]
-- p_mappings: [{ id, layout_id, column_id, fill, status, confidence, reason }]
rpc_crosswalks__save (p_crosswalk_id uuid, p_settings jsonb, p_columns jsonb, p_layouts jsonb, p_datasets jsonb, p_mappings jsonb) returns void

-- Creates the combined dataset (when the crosswalk has none) or updates it:
-- its name, raw_sql, columns (reconciled by name), and the reference
-- bindings of its coded columns. Records compiled_at and compiled_code_lists.
-- p_columns:  [{ name, data_type }] in output order
-- p_bindings: [{ column_name, dictionary_id, entry_id, code_list_id, direction }]
-- p_compiled_code_lists: [{ code_list_id, fingerprint }]
rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset (p_crosswalk_id uuid, p_dataset_id uuid, p_dataset_name text, p_raw_sql text, p_columns jsonb, p_bindings jsonb, p_compiled_code_lists jsonb) returns uuid
```

Save rules and hints: Data Sources editor on the crosswalk's workspace, and the same error for a missing crosswalk (`42501`, `crosswalk_editor_required`); the row is locked `for update`; payloads must be arrays of objects (`22023`, `crosswalk_payload_invalid`); a blank name (`23514`, `crosswalk_name_required`); a blank column name (`23514`, `column_name_required`); two column names equal ignoring case and spaces, or a column named like the source column (`source_dataset`) while `adds_source_column` (`23505`, `column_names_not_unique`); layouts present but not exactly one of them the reference (`23514`, `reference_layout_required`; a new crosswalk with no layouts can still be saved and renamed); two layouts with one signature (`23505`, `layout_signatures_not_unique`); a membership, mapping, or layout that names a layout or column not in the payload, or an id that belongs to another crosswalk (`23514`, `item_not_in_crosswalk`); a dataset id that is missing, in another workspace, or not viewable by the caller (`42501`, `dataset_not_readable`); an `entry_id` outside the workspace (`23514`, `entry_not_in_workspace`); two mappings for one layout and column (`23505`, `mappings_not_unique`); a fill without `version = 1` and a known `kind`, a `column` fill without a non-blank `source_column`, a `constant` without a string `value`, or an `expression` without a non-blank `sql` (`22023`, `fill_invalid`). Writes upsert columns, layouts, and mappings by id and delete the ones left out; memberships are upserted on `(crosswalk_id, dataset_id)` (a moved dataset keeps its membership id) and the ones left out are deleted, except that a membership whose dataset the caller cannot view is never deleted, and a save that drops a layout still holding such a membership is refused with `dataset_not_readable` (the cascade would delete it).

Combined rules and hints: Data Sources editor (`crosswalk_editor_required`, same error for a missing crosswalk); the crosswalk row is locked; a blank dataset name (`23514`, `combined_dataset_name_required`); `p_columns` empty, not an array of `{ name, data_type }`, or with names equal ignoring case (`22023`, `combined_columns_invalid`); a binding naming a column not in `p_columns` (`23514`, `binding_column_missing`); a binding whose dictionary, entry, or code list is outside the workspace, or whose entry is not in its dictionary (`23514`, `binding_not_in_workspace`). Creating (no `output_dataset_id`): `util__can_manage_workspace_settings` (`42501`, `dataset_creator_required`), then `rpc_datasets__add_virtual_dataset` with `dataset_column_input` rows (`original_name = name`, `detected_data_type = datasets__ava_data_type_to_duckdb(data_type)`, `column_idx` from order), then the bindings (`mode 'reference'`, `applied_dictionary_version` = the dictionary's version), then `output_dataset_id`. Updating: `p_dataset_id = output_dataset_id` (`23514`, `combined_dataset_mismatch`), dataset editor through `util__auth_user_can_access_resource('dataset', p_dataset_id, 'editor')` (`42501`, `dataset_editor_required`); updates `datasets.name` and `datasets__virtual.raw_sql`; keeps each `dataset_columns` row whose name matches ignoring case (updating `name`, `data_type`, `detected_data_type`, `column_idx`), inserts the new ones, deletes the rest; replaces the dataset's bindings whole with `p_bindings`. Both paths set `compiled_at = now()` and `compiled_code_lists`.

### Shared models (Tasks 6 and 7)

Paths under `shared/models/crosswalks/`. Every persisted model follows `DataDictionaryEntry/` exactly: `X.types.ts` (id brand, read type, `SupabaseCrudModelSpec`), `XParsers.ts` (`makeParserRegistry` with a snake_case `DBReadSchema` and a `ZodConsistencyTests` check), `X.ts` (namespace; re-exports parsers, and the module when there is one).

```ts
// Crosswalk/Crosswalk.types.ts
export type CrosswalkId = UUID<"Crosswalk">;
export type CrosswalkCodesOutput = Enums<"crosswalks__codes_output">;
/** A code list the combined dataset embedded, and the fingerprint of its pairs then. */
export type CrosswalkCompiledCodeList = {
  codeListId: DataDictionaryCodeList.Id;
  fingerprint: string;
};
// CrosswalkRead (Model.Base<"Crosswalk", ...>): id, workspaceId, ownerId,
//   ownerProfileId, createdAt, updatedAt, name, description: string | undefined,
//   outputDatasetId: Dataset.Id | undefined, codesOutputAs, addsSourceColumn,
//   compiledAt: string | undefined,
//   compiledCodeLists: CrosswalkCompiledCodeList[] | undefined.
// Insert: SetOptional on id, createdAt, updatedAt, ownerId, description,
//   outputDatasetId, codesOutputAs, addsSourceColumn, compiledAt, compiledCodeLists.

/** Everything `rpc_crosswalks__save` replaces, in model shape. */
export type CrosswalkSavePayload = {
  crosswalkId: CrosswalkId;
  settings: {
    name: string;
    description: string | undefined;
```

```ts
/** A change applied to a source column's values before they are cast. */
export type CrosswalkConvert =
  | { kind: "parse_date"; format: string }
  | { kind: "pad_text"; length: number }
  | { kind: "multiply"; factor: number }
  | { kind: "trim_and_fix_case"; letterCase: "keep" | "lower" | "upper" };

/**
 * How one column of the combined dataset is filled for one layout. A
 * `column` fill either converts (`convert`) or translates codes through a
 * code list (`codeListId`), never both. `holdsLabels` says the source holds
 * the list's labels rather than its codes. An `expression` names columns as
 * `{column name}` placeholders.
 */
export type CrosswalkFill =
  | {
      kind: "column";
      sourceColumn: string;
      convert: CrosswalkConvert | undefined;
      codeListId: DataDictionaryCodeList.Id | undefined;
      holdsLabels: boolean;
    }
  | { kind: "constant"; value: string }
  | { kind: "expression"; sql: string }
  | { kind: "empty" };
```

```ts
// shared/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMatch/ (pure, like DictionaryMatch)
/** A column of the combined dataset that a layout's columns are matched against. */
export type CrosswalkMatchTarget = {
  columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
  /** From the reference dataset, or a name-and-type profile for an added column. */
  profile: ColumnProfile.T;
};
/** One source column the scorer would fill a target with. */
export type CrosswalkMatchT = {
  columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
  sourceColumn: string;
  score: number;
  band: "match" | "suggestion";
  reason: "name_and_type" | "same_values";
};
/** A fill the layout starts with, and how sure the match was. */
export type CrosswalkPrefill = {
  columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
  fill: CrosswalkMapping.Fill;
  status: CrosswalkMapping.Status;
  confidence: number | undefined;
  reason: CrosswalkMapping.Reason | undefined;
};
// Module CrosswalkMatch:
//   toNameAndTypeProfiles({ datasetId; datasetName; columns: ReadonlyArray<{ name; dataType }> }): ColumnProfile.T[]
//     values undefined, counts 0: the scorer rescales without values
//   matchLayoutColumns({ targets; sources: readonly ColumnProfile.T[] }): CrosswalkMatchT[]
//     ColumnProfile.getMatchScore for every pair; keeps band match or suggestion;
//     one-to-one, best score first, ties by target order then source order;
//     reason same_values when valueScore >= 0.9 and nameScore < SUGGESTION_SCORE
//   carryOverFills({ fills: ReadonlyArray<{ columnId; fill }>; columnNames: readonly string[] }):
//     Array<{ columnId; fill }>   // a column fill whose source exists here (ignoring case, renamed to
//                                 // this layout's spelling), constants, empties, and expressions whose
//                                 // placeholders all exist here
//   chooseCodeList({ profile: ColumnProfile.T; entry: DictionaryMatch.Entry }):
//     { codeListId: DataDictionaryCodeList.Id; holdsLabels: boolean; coverage: number | undefined } | undefined
//     DictionaryMatch.getBestCodeList, falling back to the primary list holding codes when
//     values were not compared; undefined when the entry has no code list
//   suggestConvert({ source: ColumnProfile.T; target: ColumnProfile.T; targetDataType: AvaDataType.T; dateFormat: string | undefined }):
//     CrosswalkMapping.Convert | undefined
//     parse_date when the target is date or timestamp, the source is text, and dateFormat is set;
//     pad_text when every listed target value is a digit string of one length n, and the source is
//     bigint or text with listed digit values shorter than n
//   prefillLayout({ columns: ReadonlyArray<{ id; entryId: DataDictionaryEntry.Id | undefined; dataType }>;
//                   targets; sources; carriedOver?: ReadonlyArray<{ columnId; fill }>;
//                   entriesById: ReadonlyMap<string, DictionaryMatch.Entry>;
//                   dateFormatsBySourceColumn?: ReadonlyMap<string, string> }): CrosswalkPrefill[]
//     carried-over fills first (suggested, reason similar_layout); then matches for the rest:
//     band match -> confirmed, suggestion -> suggested, confidence = score; a governed column's
//     fill gets chooseCodeList, any other column's gets suggestConvert
```

```ts
//   toFillSql({ fill: CrosswalkMapping.Fill | undefined; column; codesOutputAs; codeListsById; primaryCodeListIdByEntryId }): string
//   toTranslation({ pairs; primaryPairs; holdsLabels; codesOutputAs }): ColumnConversion.T
//   getTranslationOutputs({ pairs; primaryPairs; codesOutputAs }): Array<{ pair; output: string | undefined }>
//   getGovernedDataType({ codesOutputAs; primaryPairs }): AvaDataType.T   // varchar, or bigint by ColumnConversion.getOutputDataType
//   getCodeListFingerprint(pairs): string           // "p1." + fnv1a64Hex(canonical JSON of [code, label, acceptedSpellings, isMissing])
//   toExpressionSql(sql): string                    // each {name} replaced by quoteSqlIdentifier(name)

//   ({ codeListsById, primaryCodeListIdByEntryId }), Input (CodeLists & {...}), Output, TranslationOutput.
```

The compiled shape, one branch per layout (datasets of one layout stack with `SELECT *`):

```sql
SELECT CAST("__ava_source_dataset" AS VARCHAR) AS "source_dataset",
       TRY_CAST("CaseNo" AS VARCHAR) AS "case_id",
       TRY_CAST(CASE lower(trim(CAST("GENDER" AS VARCHAR)))
         WHEN lower(trim('1')) THEN 'Male'
         WHEN lower(trim('2')) THEN 'Female'
         ELSE CAST("GENDER" AS VARCHAR) END AS VARCHAR) AS "sex",
       TRY_CAST(TRY_STRPTIME(CAST("onset_dt" AS VARCHAR), '%m/%d/%Y') AS DATE) AS "rash_onset_date",
       TRY_CAST(TRY_CAST("age_mo" AS DOUBLE) * 0.08333333333333333 AS DOUBLE) AS "age_years",
       TRY_CAST('Bronx' AS VARCHAR) AS "county",
       CAST(NULL AS BOOLEAN) AS "outbreak_associated"
FROM (
  SELECT 'Kings line list 2026-03' AS "__ava_source_dataset", * FROM "<dataset uuid>"
  UNION ALL BY NAME
  SELECT 'Kings line list 2026-04' AS "__ava_source_dataset", * FROM "<dataset uuid>"
)
UNION ALL BY NAME
SELECT …
```

Fill rendering, with `v` the quoted source column and `T` the column's `AvaDataType.toDuckDbTypeSql`:

| Fill | SQL |
| --- | --- |
| none, or `empty` | `CAST(NULL AS T)` |
| `column`, no conversion, `T` is `VARCHAR` | `CAST(v AS VARCHAR)` |
| `column`, no conversion | `TRY_CAST(v AS T)` |
| `parse_date` | `TRY_CAST(TRY_STRPTIME(CAST(v AS VARCHAR), '<format>') AS T)` |
| `pad_text` | `TRY_CAST(CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(s, '[0-9]+') AND length(s) < n THEN lpad(s, n, '0') ELSE s END AS T)` with `s = trim(CAST(v AS VARCHAR))` |
| `multiply` | `TRY_CAST(TRY_CAST(v AS DOUBLE) * <factor> AS T)`; the factor is a finite JS number rendered with `String(factor)` |
| `trim_and_fix_case` | `TRY_CAST(<lower\|upper\|>(regexp_replace(trim(CAST(v AS VARCHAR)), '\s+', ' ', 'g')) AS T)` |
| `column` with `codeListId` | `TRY_CAST(<ColumnConversion.toCaseSql of toTranslation> AS T)`; a list no longer in `codeListsById` renders as no conversion |
| `constant` | `TRY_CAST('<value>' AS T)` (`'<value>'` alone for `VARCHAR`) |
| `expression` | `TRY_CAST((<sql with each {name} replaced by quoteSqlIdentifier(name)>) AS T)` |

Translation (`toTranslation`): `L` is the fill's list, `P` the entry's primary list (or `L` when the column has no entry, its primary list is gone, or it is `L`). For each pair `p` of `L`, its counterpart is `p` itself when `L` is `P`, otherwise the first pair of `P` whose label or accepted spelling equals `p`'s label (trimmed, ignoring case). The output is the counterpart's label (or `p`'s label when there is none) in `labels` mode, and the counterpart's code in `codes` mode. When the source holds codes the conversion decodes `p.code` to the output; when it holds labels it encodes `p`'s label and accepted spellings to the output. In `codes` mode a pair with no counterpart becomes an `empty` override, so it is never passed through as a code of another list. Pairs with a blank label follow `ColumnConversion`'s rules. A governed column's type is `varchar` in `labels` mode and `ColumnConversion.getOutputDataType({ direction: "encode", pairs: P })` in `codes` mode; the draft keeps it so (Task 15).

```ts
// CV/crosswalkReducer/crosswalkReducer.types.ts
export type CrosswalkStep = "datasets" | "map" | "combine";
/** Everything the reducer reads but does not own, loaded by useCrosswalkCatalog. */
export type CrosswalkContext = {
  /** Every dataset the user can read, with its columns in column order. */
  datasetsById: ReadonlyMap<string, CrosswalkLayout.Dataset>;
  /** Dictionary entries ready to match, primary code list first. */
  entriesById: ReadonlyMap<string, DictionaryMatch.Entry>;
};
/** The reference dataset's binding for one of its columns, read when columns are seeded. */
export type ReferenceColumnBinding = {
  entryId: DataDictionaryEntry.Id;
  codeListId: DataDictionaryCodeList.Id | undefined;
  holdsLabels: boolean;
};
export type CrosswalkState = {
  draft: CrosswalkDraft.T;
  /** The draft as last saved; undefined before the first save. */
  savedDraft: CrosswalkDraft.T | undefined;
  /** Layouts whose values were read this session, so each is read once. */
  readLayoutIds: readonly CrosswalkLayout.Id[];
};
export type CrosswalkAction =
  | { type: "renamed"; name: string }
  | { type: "datasets_added"; datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[]; context: CrosswalkContext }
  | { type: "dataset_removed"; datasetId: Dataset.Id }
  | { type: "reference_chosen"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id }
  | { type: "columns_seeded"; bindingsByColumnName: ReadonlyMap<string, ReferenceColumnBinding>; context: CrosswalkContext }
  | { type: "values_read"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id; sources: readonly ColumnProfile.T[]; targets: readonly CrosswalkMatch.Target[]; dateFormatsBySourceColumn: ReadonlyMap<string, string>; context: CrosswalkContext }
  | { type: "fill_set"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id; fill: CrosswalkMapping.Fill }
  | { type: "suggestion_accepted"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id }
  | { type: "suggestion_rejected"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id }
  | { type: "suggestions_accepted"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id }
  | { type: "layout_confirmed"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id }
  | { type: "layout_skipped"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id }
  | { type: "layout_reopened"; layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id }
  | { type: "column_added"; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id; name: string; dataType: AvaDataType.T }
  | { type: "column_changed"; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id; changes: { name?: string; dataType?: AvaDataType.T; entryId?: DataDictionaryEntry.Id | null }; context: CrosswalkContext }
  | { type: "column_removed"; columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id }
  | { type: "settings_changed"; changes: { codesOutputAs?: Crosswalk.CodesOutput; addsSourceColumn?: boolean }; context: CrosswalkContext }
  | { type: "saved"; draft: CrosswalkDraft.T };
// Part B adds (and a matching entry in the reducer's HANDLERS map):
//   | { type: "meaning_matches_found"; layoutId; matches: ReadonlyArray<{ columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id; sourceColumn: string }>;
//       sources: readonly ColumnProfile.T[]; context: CrosswalkContext }
// CV/crosswalkReducer/crosswalkReducer.ts:
//   makeInitialCrosswalkState(draft: CrosswalkDraft.T, options: { isSaved: boolean }): CrosswalkState
//   crosswalkReducer(state, action): CrosswalkState
//   isCrosswalkDirty(state): boolean
//   canChangeReference(draft): boolean    // no non-reference layout is mapped
```

Reducer rules:

- The reducer mints uuids, so `useCrosswalkFlow` runs it once per dispatch and keeps the result in a ref (React may call a `useReducer` reducer twice). Steps save through `flow.dispatchAndSave(action)`, never `dispatch` followed by `save(flow.state.draft)`, which would save the draft from before the action.
- `datasets_added` ignores ids already in the draft. Each new dataset joins the layout with its key, or forms a new layout (new uuid, `buildSignature`, column names from its first dataset by name). With no reference yet, `chooseReferenceLayout` marks one (`status mapped`). With columns already seeded, every new layout is prefilled: `carryOverFills` from `findMostSimilarLayout` among the non-reference layouts, carrying only their confirmed fills, then `prefillLayout` with name-and-type targets and sources; its status follows `getStatusAfterFill`. Layouts are re-sorted (reference first, then first dataset name).
- `dataset_removed` drops the dataset; a non-reference layout left with no dataset is dropped with its mappings; the reference layout stays even when empty.
- `reference_chosen` is ignored unless `canChangeReference`. It moves `isReference` to the front, sets every other layout that is not skipped to `to_do`, clears every column and mapping, and empties `readLayoutIds`, so the next **Next** reseeds.
- `columns_seeded` (only when there are no columns): one column per reference column name in column order, named as in the reference dataset, with its type, and `entryId` from `bindingsByColumnName`; a governed column's type is `CrosswalkSql.getGovernedDataType`. The reference layout gets a confirmed `column` fill per column (`codeListId` and `holdsLabels` from the binding, or `chooseCodeList` later). Every other layout is prefilled by name and type.
- `values_read` adds the layout to `readLayoutIds` and runs `prefillLayout` with real profiles for every column whose mapping is missing or `suggested` (confirmed fills are never replaced, but a confirmed governed fill gets `chooseCodeList` from the real values unless the user chose its list: a fill set by hand has no `reason`, so a list the matcher guessed from names alone never sticks). Status follows `getStatusAfterFill` unless `mapped` or `skipped`.
- `fill_set` stores the fill as `confirmed` with no reason or confidence.
- `suggestion_accepted` confirms one; `suggestion_rejected` removes it; `suggestions_accepted` confirms every suggestion in the layout.
- `fill_set`, `suggestion_rejected`, `column_added`, and `column_removed` refresh every `to_do` or `review` layout's status with `getStatusAfterFill`; mapped, skipped, and reference layouts keep theirs.
- `layout_confirmed` confirms every mapping, gives every column without one an `empty` fill, and sets `mapped`. `layout_skipped` sets `skipped`; `layout_reopened` returns a skipped layout to `getStatusAfterFill`.
- `column_added` appends a column (no fills anywhere). `column_removed` drops it and its mappings and renumbers positions. `column_changed` with a different `entryId` re-derives the type, clears `codeListId` and `holdsLabels` from every `column` fill of that column (confirmed ones too: the old list belongs to another entry), and empties `readLayoutIds`, so each layout is read again and `values_read` gives those fills `chooseCodeList`; `null` removes the entry and every fill's `codeListId`.
- `settings_changed` with `codesOutputAs` re-derives every governed column's type.
- `saved` sets `savedDraft` to the saved draft, and sets `draft` to it only when the current draft has the same content (`CrosswalkDraft.isSameContent`). An edit made while the save was in flight stays, and the crosswalk stays dirty.

## Part A: crosswalks and the combined dataset (F136)

---

### Task 1: Enums and the crosswalks table (schema, red until Task 5)

A crosswalk is a workspace-level object shaped like a data dictionary: an owner, an owner profile validated by trigger, a workspace that cannot change, and Data Sources RLS copied word for word from `data_dictionaries`. It adds the settings the combined dataset is built with (`codes_output_as`, `adds_source_column`) and three managed columns that only `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset` writes: `output_dataset_id`, `compiled_at`, and `compiled_code_lists`.

Signed-in users write `crosswalks` directly (create, rename, delete), and the CRUD client sends whole rows, so a column-scoped grant would refuse every rename. The managed columns are guarded the way `data_dictionaries__guard_managed_columns` guards a dictionary's version: a `before insert or update` trigger refuses a signed-in user who sets or changes them, and lets the same value through. It also refuses changing `owner_id` and `owner_profile_id` after insert. The trigger checks `current_user <> 'authenticated'`, so two writers pass: the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs, which run as the function owner, and the foreign key's `on delete set null`. Postgres runs a referential action as the owner of the referencing table, so deleting the combined dataset clears `output_dataset_id` while `current_user` is `postgres`, exactly as `datasets__virtual__guard_linked_source` relies on. The test deletes the dataset as a signed-in workspace owner to prove it.

**File number.** The table references `public.datasets`, created in `10.datasets.sql`, which sorts after `10.crosswalks.sql`, so the file is `11.crosswalks.sql` (Contract note 1). Both RPCs authorize the same way, so the shared `crosswalks__authorize` helper lives here, with the table it reads.

`compiled_code_lists` holds `[{ "code_list_id": uuid, "fingerprint": text }]`. It is an array, never an object keyed by id, because the parsers run `camelCaseKeysDeep`, which would rewrite a uuid key.

**Files:**
- Create: `supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__codes_output.sql`
- Create: `supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__layout_status.sql`
- Create: `supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__mapping_status.sql`
- Create: `supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__mapping_reason.sql`
- Create: `supabase/schemas/11.crosswalks.sql`
- Test: `supabase/tests/database/permissions/rls_crosswalks.test.sql`

`crosswalks` gets the standard `authenticated` grant (select, insert, update, delete), so `exact_data_api_grants.test.sql` already expects it: that test lists only the tables that differ from the standard set. Task 2 adds the four select-only children to it.

```sql
-- The viewer gets Global Viewer and the admin Global Admin (Data Sources
-- admin). The owner and the editor get Global Editor; the owner is also
-- the workspace owner.
update public.workspace_memberships wm
set role_group_id = rg.id
from public.role_groups rg
where
  wm.workspace_id = 'c1100001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid and
  rg.workspace_id = wm.workspace_id and
  rg.is_builtin and
  rg.name = case wm.user_id
    when 'c1000002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002'::uuid then 'Global Viewer'
    when 'c1000005-0000-4000-8000-000000000005'::uuid then 'Global Admin'
    else 'Global Editor'
  end;

-- 1. A viewer reads a crosswalk in their workspace.

  output_dataset_id = 'c1450001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid,
  compiled_at = now(),

      (select compiled_at is not null from public.crosswalks where id = 'c1400001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid)
  $q$,

);
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the four enums.**

`supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__codes_output.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * How a crosswalk's combined dataset writes a column that a dictionary
 * entry governs.
 *
 * Enum values:
 *
 * `labels`: the labels of the entry's primary code list, such as Male.
 *
 * `codes`: the codes of the entry's primary code list, such as 1.
 */
create type public.crosswalks__codes_output as enum('labels', 'codes');
```

`supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__layout_status.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * How far the mapping of one crosswalk layout has got.
 *
 * Enum values:
 *
 * `to_do`: some column of the combined dataset has no fill for this layout
 * yet.
 *
 * `review`: every column has a fill, and the user has not confirmed them.
 *
 * `mapped`: the user confirmed the layout's fills. The reference layout is
 * always mapped.
 *
 * `skipped`: the user left the layout's datasets out of the combined
 * dataset.
 */
create type public.crosswalks__layout_status as enum('to_do', 'review', 'mapped', 'skipped');
```

`supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__mapping_status.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * Whether a crosswalk mapping is a guess or the user's choice.
 *
 * Enum values:
 *
 * `suggested`: filled by matching, and not yet accepted.
 *
 * `confirmed`: chosen or accepted by the user.
 */
create type public.crosswalks__mapping_status as enum('suggested', 'confirmed');
```

`supabase/schemas/00.enum.crosswalks__mapping_reason.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * Why matching suggested a crosswalk mapping. Null on a mapping the user
 * chose.
 *
 * Enum values:
 *
 * `name_and_type`: the source column's name and type resemble the target's.
 *
 * `same_values`: the source column holds the same values as the target,
 * whatever its name.
 *
 * `similar_layout`: carried over from the most similar layout already
 * mapped.
 *
 * `meaning`: an AI suggestion that the two columns mean the same thing.
 */
create type public.crosswalks__mapping_reason as enum('name_and_type', 'same_values', 'similar_layout', 'meaning');
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the table, its guards, its policies, and the shared authorize helper.**

`supabase/schemas/11.crosswalks.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * A saved mapping of many datasets with different column layouts onto one
 * set of columns, and the combined dataset that stacks them. Layouts,
 * columns, memberships, and mappings are written only through
 * `rpc_crosswalks__save`; the combined dataset and the columns that record
 * it only through `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset`.
 */
create table public.crosswalks (
  -- Primary key
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- Workspace this crosswalk belongs to
  workspace_id uuid not null references public.workspaces (id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  -- User id of the owner. A user who still owns a crosswalk cannot be
  -- deleted.
  owner_id uuid not null default auth.uid () references auth.users (id) on update cascade on delete no action,
  -- The owner's profile in this workspace
  owner_profile_id uuid not null references public.user_profiles (id) on update cascade on delete no action,
  -- Timestamp of when the crosswalk was created
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Timestamp of when the crosswalk was last updated
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Name of the crosswalk
  name text not null,
  -- Description of the crosswalk
  description text,
  -- The combined dataset: a virtual dataset that stacks every mapped
  -- dataset. Set only by `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset`. Null
  -- before the first combine, and once that dataset is deleted.
  output_dataset_id uuid references public.datasets (id) on update cascade on delete set null,
  -- Whether governed columns come out as labels or as codes
  codes_output_as public.crosswalks__codes_output not null default 'labels',
  -- Whether the combined dataset starts with a `source_dataset` column
  -- naming the dataset each row came from
  adds_source_column boolean not null default true,
  -- When the combined dataset was last created or updated. Managed.
  compiled_at timestamptz,
  -- The code lists the combined dataset embedded when it was last saved,
  -- as `[{ code_list_id, fingerprint }]`, where `fingerprint` hashes the
  -- list's pairs at that time. The browser compares fingerprints to say a
  -- list changed since. An array rather than an object keyed by id, so no
  -- key transform can rewrite an id. Managed.
  compiled_code_lists jsonb,
  -- Lets child tables use a composite foreign key that keeps them in the
  -- crosswalk's workspace.
  unique (id, workspace_id),
  constraint crosswalks__name_not_blank check (btrim(name) <> ''),
  constraint crosswalks__compiled_code_lists_is_array check (
    compiled_code_lists is null or
    jsonb_typeof(compiled_code_lists) = 'array'
  )
);

/** Prevents a crosswalk from being reassigned to another workspace. */
create or replace function public.crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change () returns trigger language plpgsql
set
  search_path = '' as $$
begin
  if new.workspace_id is distinct from old.workspace_id then
    raise exception 'crosswalk workspace_id cannot be changed'
      using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

-- Trigger-only. The trigger machinery does not consult EXECUTE.
revoke
execute on function public.crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change ()
from
  public,
  anon,
  authenticated,
  service_role;

/**
 * Refuses direct writes by a signed-in user to the columns this schema
 * manages: the combined dataset, when it was compiled, and the code lists
 * it embedded, which only `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset` sets and
 * which a new crosswalk leaves empty, and ownership, which no client flow
 * changes after insert. A whole-row update that sends the same values
 * passes. The RPCs run as the function owner, and the foreign key's
 * `on delete set null` runs as the table's owner, so both pass.
 */
create or replace function public.crosswalks__guard_managed_columns () returns trigger language plpgsql
set
  search_path = '' as $$
begin
  if current_user <> 'authenticated' then
    return new;
  end if;

  if tg_op = 'INSERT' then
    if
      new.output_dataset_id is not null or
      new.compiled_at is not null or
      new.compiled_code_lists is not null
    then
      raise exception 'a new crosswalk has no combined dataset yet'
        using errcode = '42501';
    end if;
  elsif
    new.owner_id is distinct from old.owner_id or
    new.owner_profile_id is distinct from old.owner_profile_id or
    new.output_dataset_id is distinct from old.output_dataset_id or
    new.compiled_at is distinct from old.compiled_at or
    new.compiled_code_lists is distinct from old.compiled_code_lists
  then
    raise exception 'a crosswalk''s owner and combined dataset are managed'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

revoke
execute on function public.crosswalks__guard_managed_columns ()
from
  public,
  anon,
  authenticated,
  service_role;

/** Ensures a crosswalk owner profile belongs to its owner and workspace. */
create or replace function public.crosswalks__validate_owner_profile () returns trigger language plpgsql security definer
set
  search_path = '' as $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1
    from public.user_profiles up
    where
      up.id = new.owner_profile_id and
      up.user_id = new.owner_id and
      up.workspace_id = new.workspace_id
  ) then
    raise exception 'crosswalk owner profile must match owner and workspace'
      using errcode = '23514';
  end if;

  return new;
end;
$$;

revoke
execute on function public.crosswalks__validate_owner_profile ()
from
  public,
  anon,
  authenticated,
  service_role;

/**
 * Checks that the caller is a Data Sources editor in the crosswalk's
 * workspace, then locks the crosswalk so two writes to it run one at a
 * time, and returns its workspace. A missing crosswalk and a forbidden
 * one raise the same error, so neither crosswalk RPC can be used to probe
 * for crosswalk ids. Called first by both crosswalk RPCs.
 */
create or replace function public.crosswalks__authorize (p_crosswalk_id uuid) returns uuid language plpgsql
set
  search_path = '' as $$
declare
  v_workspace_id uuid;
begin
  -- Read without a lock: the caller has not been authorized yet.
  select c.workspace_id
  into v_workspace_id
  from public.crosswalks c
  where c.id = p_crosswalk_id;

  if v_workspace_id is null or not public.util__auth_user_meets_min_app_role (
    v_workspace_id,
    'data_sources'::public.app_type,
    'editor'::public.role_level
  ) then
    raise exception 'Only Data Sources editors can change a crosswalk'
      using errcode = '42501', hint = 'crosswalk_editor_required';
  end if;

  perform 1 from public.crosswalks where id = p_crosswalk_id for update;

  if not found then
    raise exception 'Only Data Sources editors can change a crosswalk'
      using errcode = '42501', hint = 'crosswalk_editor_required';
  end if;

  return v_workspace_id;
end;
$$;

-- Runs inside the SECURITY DEFINER crosswalk RPCs and is never called
-- directly, so no Data API role gets EXECUTE.
revoke
execute on function public.crosswalks__authorize (uuid)
from
  public,
  anon,
  authenticated,
  service_role;

create trigger tr__crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change before
update of workspace_id on public.crosswalks for each row
execute function public.crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change ();

create trigger tr__crosswalks__guard_managed_columns before insert or
update on public.crosswalks for each row
execute function public.crosswalks__guard_managed_columns ();

create trigger tr__crosswalks__validate_owner_profile before insert or
update of owner_id,
owner_profile_id,
workspace_id on public.crosswalks for each row
execute function public.crosswalks__validate_owner_profile ();

create trigger tr__crosswalks__set_updated_at before
update on public.crosswalks for each row
execute function public.util__set_updated_at ();

create index idx_crosswalks__workspace_owner on public.crosswalks (workspace_id, owner_id);

create index idx_crosswalks__owner_profile_id on public.crosswalks (owner_profile_id);

-- A combined dataset's rail and Used by find the crosswalk that writes it,
-- and deleting a dataset finds the crosswalk to clear, through this index.
create index idx_crosswalks__output_dataset_id on public.crosswalks (output_dataset_id)
where
  output_dataset_id is not null;
```

Triggers on one table fire in name order, so `tr__crosswalks__guard_managed_columns` runs before `tr__crosswalks__prevent_workspace_id_change` and `tr__crosswalks__validate_owner_profile`. That is why test 16 sees the guard's `42501` and not the profile trigger's answer, and why test 11 still sees `23514`: the guard passes a workspace change, and the workspace trigger refuses it.

### Task 2: Layouts, columns, datasets, and mappings tables (schema, red until Task 5)

The four child tables hold what one crosswalk maps: its layouts (one per set of column names its datasets share), the columns of the combined dataset, which layout each dataset belongs to, and how each column is filled for each layout. Each carries `workspace_id` and `crosswalk_id` with a composite foreign key to `crosswalks (id, workspace_id)`, so a child can never sit in another workspace than its crosswalk, and the cascade removes every child with its crosswalk.

The tables reference each other through composite keys that include `crosswalk_id`: a membership's `(layout_id, crosswalk_id)` and a mapping's `(layout_id, crosswalk_id)` and `(column_id, crosswalk_id)` must name a layout and a column of the same crosswalk, so no write path, including a service-role script, can attach a mapping to another crosswalk's layout. Signed-in users get `select` only, like a dictionary's children: the only write path is `rpc_crosswalks__save` (Task 3).

Every child is visible to Data Sources viewers, except that `crosswalks__datasets` also requires view access to its dataset (`util__auth_user_can_access_resource('dataset', dataset_id, 'viewer')`). A reader never learns that a crosswalk includes a dataset they cannot open. The test makes one dataset restricted the way `rls_dataset_columns__dictionary_bindings.test.sql` does (`is_restricted = true`, owned by someone else): app roles then do not reach it, so a Global Viewer cannot see it, and its membership row is hidden from them.

**Column names and the desktop twin.** A column's name is unique per crosswalk ignoring case and surrounding spaces. The desktop twin copies indexes into SQLite, which has no `btrim` (the generator's sqlglot keeps `LOWER(BTRIM(name))`, which SQLite refuses when the twin runs), so the guarantee is split in two: `check (name = btrim(name))` keeps names trimmed, and the unique index is on `(crosswalk_id, lower(name))`. Checks never reach the twin (the generator leaves `ADD CONSTRAINT` out), and `lower` exists in SQLite (Contract note 2).

**File numbers.** Layouts depend only on `crosswalks` (11), so they are `20.`. Columns reference `data_dictionaries__entries` (`20.data_dictionaries__entries.sql`, which sorts after `20.crosswalks__columns`), and memberships reference layouts, so both are `21.`. Mappings reference layouts (20) and columns (21), so they are `22.` (Contract note 1).

```sql
-- Counts the rows of one child table of the first crosswalk that a user
-- can read.
create function pg_temp.visible_rows (p_user_id uuid, p_table text) returns integer language plpgsql as $$
declare
  v_count integer;
begin
  perform set_config('request.jwt.claims', json_build_object('sub', p_user_id, 'role', 'authenticated')::text, true);
  set local role authenticated;
  execute format(
    'select count(*)::int from public.%I where crosswalk_id = %L::uuid',
    p_table,
    'c2700001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'
  )
  into v_count;
  reset role;
  return v_count;
end;
$$;
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the layouts table.**

`supabase/schemas/20.crosswalks__layouts.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * One set of column names that one or more of a crosswalk's datasets
 * share. Datasets of one layout are mapped once, together. Exactly one
 * layout of a crosswalk with layouts is the reference, whose columns seed
 * the combined dataset's. Select-only for signed-in users; written by
 * `rpc_crosswalks__save`.
 */
create table public.crosswalks__layouts (
  -- Primary key
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- Workspace this layout belongs to, always its crosswalk's
  workspace_id uuid not null,
  -- Crosswalk this layout belongs to
  crosswalk_id uuid not null,
  -- Timestamp of when the layout was created
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Timestamp of when the layout was last updated
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- "l1." and a hash of the lowercased, trimmed, sorted column names. A
  -- dataset joins the layout whose signature its columns give.
  signature text not null,
  -- The column names of the layout's first dataset by name, in its column
  -- order
  column_names text[] not null,
  -- Whether this is the layout the combined dataset's columns come from
  is_reference boolean not null default false,
  -- How far mapping this layout has got
  status public.crosswalks__layout_status not null default 'to_do',
  unique (crosswalk_id, signature),
  -- Lets memberships and mappings use a composite foreign key that keeps
  -- them in this layout's crosswalk.
  unique (id, crosswalk_id),
  foreign key (crosswalk_id, workspace_id) references public.crosswalks (id, workspace_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  constraint crosswalks__layouts__reference_is_mapped check (
    not is_reference or
    status = 'mapped'
  ),
  constraint crosswalks__layouts__has_columns check (cardinality(column_names) > 0)
);

alter table public.crosswalks__layouts enable row level security;

-- Signed-in users read only. Writes go through the save RPC.
grant
select
  on table public.crosswalks__layouts to authenticated;

grant
select
,
  insert,
update,
delete on table public.crosswalks__layouts to service_role;

create policy "Data Sources viewers can select crosswalk layouts" on public.crosswalks__layouts for
select
  to authenticated using (
    public.util__auth_user_meets_min_app_role (
      public.crosswalks__layouts.workspace_id,
      'data_sources'::public.app_type,
      'viewer'::public.role_level
    )
  );

create trigger tr__crosswalks__layouts__set_updated_at before
update on public.crosswalks__layouts for each row
execute function public.util__set_updated_at ();

-- At most one reference layout per crosswalk.
create unique index crosswalks__layouts__one_reference on public.crosswalks__layouts (crosswalk_id)
where
  is_reference;
```

The unique `(crosswalk_id, signature)` constraint leads with `crosswalk_id`, so it also serves the composite foreign key's cascade and every lookup by crosswalk; no separate index is needed.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the columns table.**

`supabase/schemas/21.crosswalks__columns.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * One column of a crosswalk's combined dataset: its name, position, type,
 * and the dictionary entry that governs it, if any. A governed column's
 * values are translated through the entry's code lists. Select-only for
 * signed-in users; written by `rpc_crosswalks__save`.
 */
create table public.crosswalks__columns (
  -- Primary key
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- Workspace this column belongs to, always its crosswalk's
  workspace_id uuid not null,
  -- Crosswalk this column belongs to
  crosswalk_id uuid not null,
  -- Timestamp of when the column was created
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Timestamp of when the column was last updated
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- The column's name in the combined dataset, unique per crosswalk
  -- ignoring case, and stored trimmed
  name text not null,
  -- Display and output order within the crosswalk, ascending from 0
  position integer not null,
  -- The column's type in the combined dataset
  data_type public.datasets__ava_data_type not null,
  -- The dictionary entry that governs this column. Null for a column no
  -- entry governs, and once the entry is deleted.
  entry_id uuid references public.data_dictionaries__entries (id) on update cascade on delete set null,
  -- Lets mappings use a composite foreign key that keeps them in this
  -- column's crosswalk.
  unique (id, crosswalk_id),
  foreign key (crosswalk_id, workspace_id) references public.crosswalks (id, workspace_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  constraint crosswalks__columns__name_not_blank check (btrim(name) <> ''),
  -- Keeps the unique index on `lower(name)` equal to one on
  -- `lower(btrim(name))`, which the SQLite mirror could not build.
  constraint crosswalks__columns__name_trimmed check (name = btrim(name))
);

alter table public.crosswalks__columns enable row level security;

  on table public.crosswalks__columns to authenticated;

select
,
  insert,
update,
delete on table public.crosswalks__columns to service_role;

  to authenticated using (
    public.util__auth_user_meets_min_app_role (
      public.crosswalks__columns.workspace_id,
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Write the memberships table.**

`supabase/schemas/21.crosswalks__datasets.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * One dataset's membership in a crosswalk: which layout it belongs to. A
 * dataset joins the layout whose signature its columns give. Visible only
 * to Data Sources viewers who can also view the dataset, so a reader never
 * learns about a dataset they cannot open. Select-only for signed-in
 * users; written by `rpc_crosswalks__save`, which never removes a
 * membership whose dataset the caller cannot view.
 */
create table public.crosswalks__datasets (
  -- Primary key
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- Workspace this membership belongs to, always its crosswalk's
  workspace_id uuid not null,
  -- Crosswalk the dataset belongs to
  crosswalk_id uuid not null,
  -- Timestamp of when the dataset joined the crosswalk
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- The dataset. Leaves every crosswalk when it is deleted.
  dataset_id uuid not null references public.datasets (id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  -- The layout the dataset belongs to, in the same crosswalk
  layout_id uuid not null,
  unique (crosswalk_id, dataset_id),
  foreign key (crosswalk_id, workspace_id) references public.crosswalks (id, workspace_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  foreign key (layout_id, crosswalk_id) references public.crosswalks__layouts (id, crosswalk_id) on update cascade on delete cascade
);

alter table public.crosswalks__datasets enable row level security;

-- Signed-in users read only. Writes go through the save RPC.
grant
select
  on table public.crosswalks__datasets to authenticated;

grant
select
,
  insert,
update,
delete on table public.crosswalks__datasets to service_role;

-- Memberships follow their dataset as well as the crosswalk: a reader who
-- cannot view a dataset never sees that a crosswalk includes it.
create policy "Dataset viewers can select their crosswalk memberships" on public.crosswalks__datasets for
select
  to authenticated using (
    public.util__auth_user_meets_min_app_role (
      public.crosswalks__datasets.workspace_id,
      'data_sources'::public.app_type,
      'viewer'::public.role_level
    ) and
    public.util__auth_user_can_access_resource (
      'dataset'::public.resource_type,
      public.crosswalks__datasets.dataset_id,
      'viewer'::public.role_level
    )
  );

-- Deleting a dataset, and a combined dataset's staleness lookups, find its
-- memberships through this index.
create index idx_crosswalks__datasets__dataset_id on public.crosswalks__datasets (dataset_id);

-- Deleting a layout finds its memberships through this index.
create index idx_crosswalks__datasets__layout_id on public.crosswalks__datasets (layout_id);
```

The policy requires both Data Sources viewer and dataset viewer; its name stays under Postgres's 63-character identifier limit. `crosswalks__datasets` has no `updated_at`: a membership changes only its layout, and only through the save.

`supabase/schemas/22.crosswalks__mappings.sql`:

```sql
/**
 * How one column of a crosswalk's combined dataset is filled for one
 * layout: from a source column (optionally converted, or translated
 * through a code list), a fixed value, a Combine expression, or left
 * empty. `fill` is a versioned object the browser parses (version 1:
 * `{ version, kind, ... }`). Select-only for signed-in users; written by
 * `rpc_crosswalks__save`.
 */
create table public.crosswalks__mappings (
  -- Primary key
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- Workspace this mapping belongs to, always its crosswalk's
  workspace_id uuid not null,
  -- Crosswalk this mapping belongs to
  crosswalk_id uuid not null,
  -- Timestamp of when the mapping was created
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- Timestamp of when the mapping was last updated
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  -- The layout whose datasets this fill reads
  layout_id uuid not null,
  -- The combined dataset's column this fill writes
  column_id uuid not null,
  -- How the column is filled, as a versioned object
  fill jsonb not null,
  -- Whether the fill is a guess or the user's choice
  status public.crosswalks__mapping_status not null default 'suggested',
  -- How sure matching was, from 0 to 1. Null for a fill the user chose.
  confidence numeric,
  -- Why matching suggested this fill. Null for a fill the user chose.
  reason public.crosswalks__mapping_reason,
  unique (layout_id, column_id),
  foreign key (crosswalk_id, workspace_id) references public.crosswalks (id, workspace_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  -- The composite keys keep the layout and the column in this crosswalk.
  foreign key (layout_id, crosswalk_id) references public.crosswalks__layouts (id, crosswalk_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  foreign key (column_id, crosswalk_id) references public.crosswalks__columns (id, crosswalk_id) on update cascade on delete cascade,
  constraint crosswalks__mappings__confidence_range check (
    confidence is null or
    confidence between 0 and 1
  ),
  constraint crosswalks__mappings__fill_is_object check (jsonb_typeof(fill) = 'object')
);
```

### Task 3: `rpc_crosswalks__save` (schema, red until Task 5)

The browser edits a whole crosswalk as one draft and saves it whole, so one RPC replaces a crosswalk's settings, columns, layouts, memberships, and mappings in one transaction. It follows `rpc_data_dictionaries__save`: SECURITY DEFINER with `search_path = ''`, authorization against the crosswalk's own workspace before anything else is read, one error for a missing and a forbidden crosswalk, a row lock so two saves run one at a time, a set of check helpers that raise stable hints, and writers that upsert by id and delete what the payload leaves out. Every helper is plain (`search_path = ''`, no SECURITY DEFINER) and revoke-only: it runs inside the RPC as the function owner.

Three rules need a word:

- **Hidden memberships are never deleted.** `crosswalks__datasets` hides a membership whose dataset the caller cannot view, so the draft never contains it. Memberships are upserted on `(crosswalk_id, dataset_id)` (a moved dataset keeps its membership id), and the delete of left-out memberships skips any dataset the caller cannot view. A layout holding such a membership cannot be dropped either, because the cascade would delete it: that save is refused with `dataset_not_readable` (Contract note 4).
- **A crosswalk with no layouts saves.** A new crosswalk can be renamed before any dataset is added, so `reference_layout_required` applies only to a non-empty layout set: exactly one reference, and it is `mapped` (Contract note 3).
- **Swaps never meet a unique index halfway.** Writers park the saved names and signatures under `'~' || id`, and clear `is_reference`, before upserting, the way `data_dictionaries__write_entries` parks entry names. A save that swaps two column names, swaps two signatures, or moves the reference therefore never trips `crosswalks__columns__name_unique`, `(crosswalk_id, signature)`, or `crosswalks__layouts__one_reference` partway through.

The payload is checked for shape before anything casts it (a uuid pattern, enum ranges, integer positions), so a malformed payload raises `crosswalk_payload_invalid` instead of a bare cast error (Contract note 6). The column named like the source column is `source_dataset`, the value of `CrosswalkModule.SOURCE_COLUMN_NAME`; the SQL repeats the literal, and the comment names the constant so the two are kept together.

```sql
\set ON_ERROR_STOP on

/**
 * `rpc_crosswalks__save` replaces one crosswalk's settings, columns,
 * layouts, dataset memberships, and mappings in one transaction. Only a
 * Data Sources editor can call it; every refusal raises a stable `hint`
 * and changes nothing. Ids stay stable across saves, a dropped layout
 * takes its mappings with it, and a membership whose dataset the caller
 * cannot view survives every save.
 */
begin;

set search_path to extensions, public;

create function pg_temp.error_hint (p_sql text) returns text language plpgsql as $$
declare
  v_hint text;
begin
  execute p_sql;
  return 'no error';
exception
  when others then
    get stacked diagnostics v_hint = pg_exception_hint;
    return v_hint;
end;
$$;

-- The first save's payload, one function per argument. Tests change one
-- piece with `jsonb_set` or `||` and pass the rest as they are.
create function pg_temp.base_settings () returns jsonb language sql as $$
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'name', 'Kings and Queens',
    'description', 'Every borough line list on one layout.',
    'codes_output_as', 'labels',
    'adds_source_column', true
  );
$$;

create function pg_temp.base_columns () returns jsonb language sql as $$

    {"id":"c4720001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","name":"case_id","position":0,"data_type":"varchar","entry_id":null},

    {"id":"c4720003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","name":"onset","position":2,"data_type":"date","entry_id":null}
  ]'::jsonb;
$$;

create function pg_temp.base_layouts () returns jsonb language sql as $$

    {"id":"c4710001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","signature":"l1.0000000000000001","column_names":["case_id","sex","onset"],"is_reference":true,"status":"mapped"},
    {"id":"c4710002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","signature":"l1.0000000000000002","column_names":["CaseNo","GENDER","onset_dt"],"is_reference":false,"status":"to_do"},
    {"id":"c4710003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","signature":"l1.0000000000000003","column_names":["caseno"],"is_reference":false,"status":"review"}
  ]'::jsonb;
$$;

create function pg_temp.base_datasets () returns jsonb language sql as $$
  select '[
    {"dataset_id":"c4450001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","layout_id":"c4710002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"},

    {"dataset_id":"c4450003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","layout_id":"c4710001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"}
  ]'::jsonb;
$$;

create function pg_temp.base_mappings () returns jsonb language sql as $$
  select '[
    {"id":"c4730001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","layout_id":"c4710001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","column_id":"c4720001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","fill":{"version":1,"kind":"column","source_column":"case_id","convert":null,"code_list_id":null,"holds_labels":false},"status":"confirmed","confidence":null,"reason":null},

    {"id":"c4730003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","layout_id":"c4710002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","column_id":"c4720002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","fill":{"version":1,"kind":"column","source_column":"GENDER","convert":null,"code_list_id":"c4500001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","holds_labels":false},"status":"confirmed","confidence":null,"reason":null},
    {"id":"c4730004-0000-4000-8000-000000000004","layout_id":"c4710003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","column_id":"c4720001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001","fill":{"version":1,"kind":"column","source_column":"caseno","convert":null,"code_list_id":null,"holds_labels":false},"status":"suggested","confidence":0.8,"reason":"similar_layout"},
    {"id":"c4730005-0000-4000-8000-000000000005","layout_id":"c4710002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002","column_id":"c4720003-0000-4000-8000-000000000003","fill":{"version":1,"kind":"column","source_column":"onset_dt","convert":{"kind":"parse_date","format":"%m/%d/%Y"},"code_list_id":null,"holds_labels":false},"status":"confirmed","confidence":null,"reason":null}
  ]'::jsonb;
$$;

-- Runs one save and returns its hint, or 'no error'. By default the
-- editor saves the first payload into the crosswalk under test.
create function pg_temp.save (
  p_settings jsonb default pg_temp.base_settings (),
  p_columns jsonb default pg_temp.base_columns (),
  p_layouts jsonb default pg_temp.base_layouts (),
  p_datasets jsonb default pg_temp.base_datasets (),
  p_mappings jsonb default pg_temp.base_mappings (),
  p_user_id uuid default 'c4000002-0000-4000-8000-000000000002'::uuid,
  p_crosswalk_id uuid default 'c4700001-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'::uuid
) returns text language plpgsql as $$
begin
  return pg_temp.error_hint (format(
    $s$
      set local role authenticated;
      select set_config('request.jwt.claims', %L, true);
      select public.rpc_crosswalks__save (%L::uuid, %L::jsonb, %L::jsonb, %L::jsonb, %L::jsonb, %L::jsonb);
    $s$,
    json_build_object('sub', p_user_id, 'role', 'authenticated')::text,
    p_crosswalk_id,
    p_settings,
    p_columns,
    p_layouts,
    p_datasets,
    p_mappings
  ));
end;
$$;
```
