`shared/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkSql/CrosswalkSqlModule/CrosswalkSqlModule.ts`:

```ts
import { quoteSqlIdentifier, quoteSqlLiteral } from "@avandar/utils/sql";
import { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping.ts";
import { ColumnConversion } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/ColumnConversion/ColumnConversion.ts";
import { AvaDataType } from "$/models/datasets/AvaDataType/AvaDataType.ts";
import { fnv1a64Hex } from "$/utils/fnv1a64Hex/fnv1a64Hex.ts";
import type { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk.ts";
import type {
  CrosswalkSqlCodeLists,
  CrosswalkSqlColumn,
  CrosswalkSqlInput,
  CrosswalkSqlLayout,
  CrosswalkSqlOutput,
  CrosswalkSqlTranslationOutput,
} from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkSql/CrosswalkSql.types.ts";
import type { DataDictionaryCodeList } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryCodeList/DataDictionaryCodeList.ts";

/** The column each stacked dataset's name is selected as, then renamed. */
const SOURCE_ALIAS = "__ava_source_dataset";

/** The pair format `getCodeListFingerprint` hashes. */
const FINGERPRINT_PREFIX = "p1.";

type Pairs = readonly DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair[];
type Fill = CrosswalkMapping.Fill;
type ColumnFill = Extract<Fill, { kind: "column" }>;
type Convert = CrosswalkMapping.Convert;

/** A fill's SQL and the code lists it embedded. */
type FillSql = { sql: string; codeListIds: string[] };

function _normalize(text: string): string {
  return text.trim().toLowerCase();
}

/** A locale-free order, so the same ids sort the same everywhere. */
function _compareCodePoints(textA: string, textB: string): number {
  if (textA === textB) {
    return 0;
  }
  return textA < textB ? -1 : 1;
}

/** The first primary pair whose label or accepted spelling is `label`. */
function _findCounterpart(
  label: string,
  primaryPairs: Pairs,
): DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair | undefined {
  const key = _normalize(label);
  if (key === "") {
    return undefined;
  }
  return primaryPairs.find((primaryPair) => {
    return [primaryPair.label, ...primaryPair.acceptedSpellings].some(
      (spelling) => {
        return _normalize(spelling) === key;
      },
    );
  });
}

/**
 * What each pair of a fill's code list becomes in the combined dataset: the
 * label (labels mode) or code (codes mode) of its counterpart in the
 * primary list, so two codings of one entry come out alike. A pair's
 * counterpart is itself when `pairs` is `primaryPairs` (pass the same
 * array), otherwise the first primary pair whose label or accepted
 * spelling matches its label. With no counterpart, labels mode keeps the
 * pair's own label and codes mode outputs nothing.
 */
function getTranslationOutputs(
  options: Readonly<{
    pairs: Pairs;
    primaryPairs: Pairs;
    codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
  }>,
): CrosswalkSqlTranslationOutput[] {
  const isPrimary = options.pairs === options.primaryPairs;
  return options.pairs.map((pair) => {
    const counterpart = isPrimary
      ? pair
      : _findCounterpart(pair.label, options.primaryPairs);
    if (options.codesOutputAs === "codes") {
      return { pair, output: counterpart?.code };
    }
    return { pair, output: counterpart?.label ?? pair.label };
  });
}

function _getSpellings(pair: DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair): string[] {
  return [pair.label, ...pair.acceptedSpellings].filter((spelling) => {
    return spelling.trim() !== "";
  });
}

function _toTranslatedPair(
  pair: DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair,
  output: string,
  holdsLabels: boolean,
): DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair {
  return holdsLabels
    ? { ...pair, code: output }
    : { ...pair, label: output, acceptedSpellings: [] };
}

/**
 * The conversion that turns a source column holding a code list's codes
 * (or its labels, with `holdsLabels`) into what the combined dataset
 * outputs, per `getTranslationOutputs`. In codes mode a pair with no
 * counterpart becomes empty rather than passing through as a code of
 * another list; in labels mode a pair whose output is blank passes
 * through, as `ColumnConversion` treats a blank label. Its output stays
 * text; the caller casts it.
 */
function toTranslation(
  options: Readonly<{
    pairs: Pairs;
    primaryPairs: Pairs;
    holdsLabels: boolean;
    codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
  }>,
): ColumnConversion.T {
  const outputs = getTranslationOutputs(options);
  const pairs = outputs.flatMap(({ pair, output }) => {
    return output === undefined || output.trim() === ""
      ? []
      : [_toTranslatedPair(pair, output, options.holdsLabels)];
  });
  const overrides = outputs.flatMap(({ pair, output }) => {
    if (output !== undefined) {
      return [];
    }
    const values = options.holdsLabels ? _getSpellings(pair) : [pair.code];
    return values.map((value) => {
      return { value, action: "empty" as const };
    });
  });
  return {
    // A translation fills a crosswalk column, not a dataset column.
    datasetColumnId: "",
    direction: options.holdsLabels ? "encode" : "decode",
    pairs,
    isOrdered: false,
    overrides,
    keepsOriginalAs: undefined,
    outputDataType: "varchar",
    inputDataType: undefined,
  };
}

/**
 * The type a column an entry governs takes: text in labels mode, and in
 * codes mode `bigint` when every primary code is a whole number, as
 * `ColumnConversion.getOutputDataType` decides for an encoded column.
 */
function getGovernedDataType(
  options: Readonly<{
    codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
    primaryPairs: Pairs;
  }>,
): AvaDataType.T {
  return options.codesOutputAs === "labels"
    ? "varchar"
    : ColumnConversion.getOutputDataType({
        direction: "encode",
        pairs: options.primaryPairs,
      });
}

/**
 * A fingerprint of a code list's pairs: the same for the same codes,
 * labels, spellings, and missing flags in the same order, whatever object
 * holds them. The combined dataset records one per embedded list, and a
 * changed fingerprint means its SQL is out of date.
 */
function getCodeListFingerprint(pairs: Pairs): string {
  const canonical = JSON.stringify(
    pairs.map((pair) => {
      return [pair.code, pair.label, pair.acceptedSpellings, pair.isMissing];
    }),
  );
  return `${FINGERPRINT_PREFIX}${fnv1a64Hex(canonical)}`;
}

function _toCastSql(valueSql: string, typeSql: string): string {
  return `TRY_CAST(${valueSql} AS ${typeSql})`;
}

function _toConvertedSql(convert: Convert, valueSql: string): string {
  const textSql = `CAST(${valueSql} AS VARCHAR)`;
  if (convert.kind === "parse_date") {
    return `TRY_STRPTIME(${textSql}, ${quoteSqlLiteral(convert.format)})`;
  }
  if (convert.kind === "pad_text") {
    if (!Number.isInteger(convert.length) || convert.length < 1) {
      throw new Error(
        `A pad length must be a positive integer, not ${convert.length}`,
      );
    }
    const trimmedSql = `trim(${textSql})`;
    return `CASE WHEN regexp_full_match(${trimmedSql}, '[0-9]+') AND length(${trimmedSql}) < ${convert.length} THEN lpad(${trimmedSql}, ${convert.length}, '0') ELSE ${trimmedSql} END`;
  }
  if (convert.kind === "multiply") {
    if (!Number.isFinite(convert.factor)) {
      throw new Error(
        `A multiply factor must be finite, not ${convert.factor}`,
      );
    }
    return `TRY_CAST(${valueSql} AS DOUBLE) * ${String(convert.factor)}`;
  }
  const squashedSql = `regexp_replace(trim(${textSql}), '\\s+', ' ', 'g')`;
  return convert.letterCase === "keep"
    ? squashedSql
    : `${convert.letterCase}(${squashedSql})`;
}

function _getPrimaryCodeListId(
  column: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlColumn>,
  codeListId: string,
  codeLists: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlCodeLists>,
): string {
  const primaryId =
    column.entryId === undefined
      ? undefined
      : codeLists.primaryCodeListIdByEntryId.get(column.entryId);
  return primaryId !== undefined && codeLists.codeListsById.has(primaryId)
    ? primaryId
    : codeListId;
}

function _toColumnFillSql(
  fill: ColumnFill,
  column: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlColumn>,
  options: Readonly<
    CrosswalkSqlCodeLists & { codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput }
  >,
): FillSql {
  const valueSql = quoteSqlIdentifier(fill.sourceColumn);
  const typeSql = AvaDataType.toDuckDbTypeSql(column.dataType);
  const codeList =
    fill.codeListId === undefined
      ? undefined
      : options.codeListsById.get(fill.codeListId);
  if (fill.codeListId !== undefined && codeList !== undefined) {
    const primaryId = _getPrimaryCodeListId(column, fill.codeListId, options);
    const primaryPairs =
      options.codeListsById.get(primaryId)?.pairs ?? codeList.pairs;
    const conversion = toTranslation({
      pairs: codeList.pairs,
      primaryPairs,
      holdsLabels: fill.holdsLabels,
      codesOutputAs: options.codesOutputAs,
    });
    return {
      sql: _toCastSql(
        ColumnConversion.toCaseSql({ valueSql, conversion }),
        typeSql,
      ),
      codeListIds: [...new Set([fill.codeListId, primaryId])],
    };
  }
  if (fill.convert !== undefined) {
    return {
      sql: _toCastSql(_toConvertedSql(fill.convert, valueSql), typeSql),
      codeListIds: [],
    };
  }
  const sql =
    typeSql === "VARCHAR"
      ? `CAST(${valueSql} AS VARCHAR)`
      : _toCastSql(valueSql, typeSql);
  return { sql, codeListIds: [] };
}

/**
 * A Combine expression as SQL: each `{column name}` placeholder replaced by
 * the column's quoted identifier. Use it to check an expression exactly as
 * the combined dataset will run it.
 */
function toExpressionSql(sql: string): string {
  return sql.replace(
    CrosswalkMapping.COMBINE_PLACEHOLDER_PATTERN,
    (_placeholder, name: string) => {
      return quoteSqlIdentifier(name.trim());
    },
  );
}

function _toFillSql(
  options: Readonly<
    CrosswalkSqlCodeLists & {
      fill: Fill | undefined;
      column: CrosswalkSqlColumn;
      codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
    }
  >,
): FillSql {
  const { fill, column } = options;
  const typeSql = AvaDataType.toDuckDbTypeSql(column.dataType);
  if (fill === undefined || fill.kind === "empty") {
    return { sql: `CAST(NULL AS ${typeSql})`, codeListIds: [] };
  }
  if (fill.kind === "column") {
    return _toColumnFillSql(fill, column, options);
  }
  if (fill.kind === "constant") {
    const literalSql = quoteSqlLiteral(fill.value);
    const sql =
      typeSql === "VARCHAR" ? literalSql : _toCastSql(literalSql, typeSql);
    return { sql, codeListIds: [] };
  }
  return {
    sql: _toCastSql(`(${toExpressionSql(fill.sql)})`, typeSql),
    codeListIds: [],
  };
}

/**
 * The SQL expression that fills one column of the combined dataset from one
 * layout's datasets, cast to the column's type so a bad value becomes empty
 * instead of failing the query. A column with no fill is a typed NULL. A
 * code list no longer in `codeListsById` leaves the values unconverted.
 * Use it wherever a fill's result is shown, such as an example of a fill's
 * before and after values, so it is exactly what the combined dataset runs.
 */
function toFillSql(
  options: Readonly<
    CrosswalkSqlCodeLists & {
      fill: Fill | undefined;
      column: CrosswalkSqlColumn;
      codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
    }
  >,
): string {
  return _toFillSql(options).sql;
}

function _toDatasetsSql(
  layout: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlLayout>,
  hasSourceColumn: boolean,
): string {
  return layout.datasets
    .map((dataset) => {
      const sourceSql = hasSourceColumn
        ? `${quoteSqlLiteral(dataset.name)} AS ${quoteSqlIdentifier(SOURCE_ALIAS)}, `
        : "";
      return `SELECT ${sourceSql}* FROM ${quoteSqlIdentifier(dataset.id)}`;
    })
    .join("\n  UNION ALL BY NAME\n  ");
}

function _toBranch(
  layout: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlLayout>,
  input: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlInput>,
): FillSql {
  const fillSqls = input.columns.map((column) => {
    const fillSql = _toFillSql({
      ...input,
      fill: layout.fillsByColumnId.get(column.id),
      column,
    });
    return {
      ...fillSql,
      sql: `${fillSql.sql} AS ${quoteSqlIdentifier(column.name)}`,
    };
  });
  const sourceItems =
    input.sourceColumnName === undefined
      ? []
      : [
          `CAST(${quoteSqlIdentifier(SOURCE_ALIAS)} AS VARCHAR) AS ${quoteSqlIdentifier(input.sourceColumnName)}`,
        ];
  const selectItems = [
    ...sourceItems,
    ...fillSqls.map((fillSql) => {
      return fillSql.sql;
    }),
  ];
  const datasetsSql = _toDatasetsSql(
    layout,
    input.sourceColumnName !== undefined,
  );
  return {
    sql: `SELECT ${selectItems.join(",\n  ")}\nFROM (\n  ${datasetsSql}\n)`,
    codeListIds: fillSqls.flatMap((fillSql) => {
      return fillSql.codeListIds;
    }),
  };
}

/**
 * The combined dataset's SQL: one `SELECT` per layout, every output
 * aliased, stacked with `UNION ALL BY NAME`. A layout's datasets share
 * their column names, so they stack first with `SELECT *` under each
 * dataset's name. Layouts and datasets stay in the given order.
 *
 * @throws `Error("crosswalk-nothing-to-combine")` when no layout has a
 * dataset, or there is no column to output.
 */
function compile(input: Readonly<CrosswalkSqlInput>): CrosswalkSqlOutput {
  const layouts = input.layouts.filter((layout) => {
    return layout.datasets.length > 0;
  });
  const columns = [
    ...(input.sourceColumnName === undefined
      ? []
      : [{ name: input.sourceColumnName, dataType: "varchar" as const }]),
    ...input.columns.map((column) => {
      return { name: column.name, dataType: column.dataType };
    }),
  ];
  if (layouts.length === 0 || columns.length === 0) {
    throw new Error("crosswalk-nothing-to-combine");
  }
  const branches = layouts.map((layout) => {
    return _toBranch(layout, input);
  });
  const usedCodeListIds = branches.flatMap((branch) => {
    return branch.codeListIds;
  });
  return {
    sql: branches
      .map((branch) => {
        return branch.sql;
      })
      .join("\nUNION ALL BY NAME\n"),
    columns,
    usedCodeListIds: [...new Set(usedCodeListIds)].sort(_compareCodePoints),
  };
}

/**
 * Pure rules for compiling a crosswalk into its combined dataset's SQL:
 * each fill's expression, the translation that reconciles codings to the
 * primary list, a governed column's type, and the fingerprint the stale
 * banner compares. Builds SQL text only; it runs nothing.
 */
export const CrosswalkSqlModule = {
  SOURCE_ALIAS,
  compile,
  toFillSql,
  toExpressionSql,
  toTranslation,
  getTranslationOutputs,
  getGovernedDataType,
  getCodeListFingerprint,
};
```

### Task 11: The combined SQL on real DuckDB (executed)

Task 10's unit tests pin the SQL text; this test pins what it does. It compiles three layouts and runs the result on an in-memory `@duckdb/node-api` instance from `withDuckDb`, with each dataset as a table named by its id, the way QETL registers a dataset. Kings has two datasets, the second named `Kings O'Brien $& --` and spelling its columns `caseno`, `gender`, `ONSET_DT` (quoted identifiers and `UNION ALL BY NAME` both match ignoring case); Kings decodes `GENDER` with the primary list, reads `onset_dt` as a date (`13/45/2026` becomes NULL), pads `zip` (`501` becomes `00501`, `1234567` is never truncated), and multiplies `age_mo` by 1/12. Queens codes sex with a second list whose `X` has no primary counterpart; Bronx holds sex as labels (` female `) and builds its case id with `concat({Case No}, '-', {year})`. The test asserts every row, every column type, and codes mode reconciling to the primary codes with `X` becoming NULL and the column `BIGINT`.

The file sits in `src/lib/crosswalks/__tests__/` and keeps the module's name: an executed test of a `shared/` module cannot live under `shared/` (it imports the Node-only harness), so `docs/rules/testing.md` puts it in a `__tests__/` under `src/`.

It passes on its first run, since it exercises Task 10's code. To see it fail for a real reason, change `` `TRY_STRPTIME( `` to `` `strptime( `` in `CrosswalkSqlModule.ts`: every case fails with `Invalid Input Error: Could not parse string "13/45/2026"`. Revert before committing.

`src/lib/crosswalks/__tests__/CrosswalkSql.executed.test.ts`:

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { CrosswalkSql } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkSql/CrosswalkSql";
import { withDuckDb } from "../../../../tests/integration/queries/executedDuckDb";
import type { CrosswalkColumn } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkColumn/CrosswalkColumn";
import type { CrosswalkLayout } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkLayout/CrosswalkLayout";
import type { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import type { DataDictionaryCodeList } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryCodeList/DataDictionaryCodeList";
import type { DataDictionaryEntry } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryEntry/DataDictionaryEntry";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

/*
 * The combined dataset's SQL, compiled from three layouts and run on real
 * DuckDB. Kings has two datasets, one with a hostile name; Queens codes sex
 * with a second list; Bronx holds sex as labels and builds its case id with
 * a Combine expression.
 */

const KINGS_MARCH = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111" as Dataset.Id;
const KINGS_HOSTILE = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222" as Dataset.Id;
const QUEENS = "33333333-3333-4333-8333-333333333333" as Dataset.Id;
const BRONX = "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444" as Dataset.Id;

const LIST_129 =
  "55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555" as DataDictionaryCodeList.Id;
const LIST_MFU =
  "66666666-6666-4666-8666-666666666666" as DataDictionaryCodeList.Id;
const ENTRY_SEX =
  "77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777" as DataDictionaryEntry.Id;

/** Each dataset as a table named by its id, the way QETL registers it. */
const TABLES_SQL = [
  `CREATE TABLE "${KINGS_MARCH}" AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    ('K1', 1, '03/02/2026', 501, 24),
    ('K2', 2, '13/45/2026', 10451, 6)
  ) AS t("CaseNo", "GENDER", onset_dt, zip, age_mo)`,
  `CREATE TABLE "${KINGS_HOSTILE}" AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    ('K3', 9, '04/01/2026', 1234567, 18)
  ) AS t(caseno, gender, "ONSET_DT", zip, age_mo)`,
  `CREATE TABLE "${QUEENS}" AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    ('Q1', 'M', DATE '2026-03-05', '11368'),
    ('Q2', 'X', DATE '2026-03-06', '11101')
  ) AS t(case_id, sex, rash_onset, zip_code)`,
  `CREATE TABLE "${BRONX}" AS SELECT * FROM (VALUES
    (7, 2026, ' female '),
    (8, 2026, 'Male')
  ) AS t("Case No", "Year", sex)`,
];

function _pair(code: string, label: string): DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair {
  return { code, label, acceptedSpellings: [], isMissing: false };
}

const CODE_LISTS: CrosswalkSql.CodeLists = {
  codeListsById: new Map([
    [
      LIST_129,
      {
        pairs: [
          _pair("1", "Male"),
          _pair("2", "Female"),
          _pair("9", "Unknown"),
        ],
      },
    ],
    [
      LIST_MFU,
      {
        pairs: [_pair("M", "Male"), _pair("F", "Female"), _pair("X", "Other")],
      },
    ],
  ]),
  primaryCodeListIdByEntryId: new Map([
    [ENTRY_SEX as string, LIST_129 as string],
  ]),
};

function _column(
  name: string,
  dataType: CrosswalkSql.Column["dataType"],
  entryId?: DataDictionaryEntry.Id,
): CrosswalkSql.Column {
  return { id: `col-${name}` as CrosswalkColumn.Id, name, dataType, entryId };
}

function _columnFill(
  sourceColumn: string,
  changes: Partial<Extract<CrosswalkMapping.Fill, { kind: "column" }>> = {},
): CrosswalkMapping.Fill {
  return {
    kind: "column",
    sourceColumn,
    convert: undefined,
    codeListId: undefined,
    holdsLabels: false,
    ...changes,
  };
}

function _layout(
  layoutId: string,
  datasets: CrosswalkSql.Layout["datasets"],
  fills: Record<string, CrosswalkMapping.Fill>,
): CrosswalkSql.Layout {
  return {
    layoutId: layoutId as CrosswalkLayout.Id,
    datasets,
    fillsByColumnId: new Map(
      Object.entries(fills).map(([name, fill]) => {
        return [`col-${name}`, fill] as const;
      }),
    ),
  };
}

const LAYOUTS = [
  _layout(
    "layout-kings",
    [
      { id: KINGS_MARCH, name: "Kings 2026-03" },
      { id: KINGS_HOSTILE, name: "Kings O'Brien $& --" },
    ],
    {
      case_id: _columnFill("CaseNo"),
      sex: _columnFill("GENDER", { codeListId: LIST_129 }),
      rash_onset_date: _columnFill("onset_dt", {
        convert: { kind: "parse_date", format: "%m/%d/%Y" },
      }),
      zip: _columnFill("zip", { convert: { kind: "pad_text", length: 5 } }),
      age_years: _columnFill("age_mo", {
        convert: { kind: "multiply", factor: 1 / 12 },
      }),
      county: { kind: "constant", value: "Kings" },
    },
  ),
  _layout("layout-queens", [{ id: QUEENS, name: "Queens 2026-03" }], {
    case_id: _columnFill("case_id"),
    sex: _columnFill("sex", { codeListId: LIST_MFU }),
    rash_onset_date: _columnFill("rash_onset"),
    zip: _columnFill("zip_code"),
    county: { kind: "constant", value: "Queens" },
    outbreak_associated: { kind: "empty" },
  }),
  _layout("layout-bronx", [{ id: BRONX, name: "Bronx 2026-03" }], {
    case_id: { kind: "expression", sql: "concat({Case No}, '-', {year})" },
    sex: _columnFill("sex", { codeListId: LIST_129, holdsLabels: true }),
  }),
];

function _compile(codesOutputAs: "labels" | "codes"): CrosswalkSql.Output {
  return CrosswalkSql.compile({
    ...CODE_LISTS,
    codesOutputAs,
    sourceColumnName: "source_dataset",
    columns: [
      _column("case_id", "varchar"),
      _column(
        "sex",
        codesOutputAs === "labels" ? "varchar" : "bigint",
        ENTRY_SEX,
      ),
      _column("rash_onset_date", "date"),
      _column("zip", "varchar"),
      _column("age_years", "double"),
      _column("county", "varchar"),
      _column("outbreak_associated", "boolean"),
    ],
    layouts: LAYOUTS,
  });
}

type CombinedRead = {
  rows: Array<Record<string, unknown>>;
  types: Record<string, string>;
};

async function _readCombined(sql: string): Promise<CombinedRead> {
  return await withDuckDb(async (connection) => {
    for (const tableSql of TABLES_SQL) {
      await connection.run(tableSql);
    }
    await connection.run(`CREATE VIEW combined AS ${sql}`);
    const rows = await connection.runAndReadAll(
      `SELECT * FROM combined ORDER BY case_id`,
    );
    const described = await connection.runAndReadAll(
      `SELECT column_name, column_type FROM (DESCRIBE combined)`,
    );
    return {
      rows: rows.getRowObjectsJson() as Array<Record<string, unknown>>,
      types: Object.fromEntries(
        described.getRowObjectsJson().map((row) => {
          return [String(row.column_name), String(row.column_type)];
        }),
      ),
    };
  });
}

describe("CrosswalkSql.compile on DuckDB", () => {
  it("stacks every layout into the combined columns, in labels mode", async () => {
    const { rows } = await _readCombined(_compile("labels").sql);

    expect(rows).toEqual([
      {
        source_dataset: "Bronx 2026-03",
        case_id: "7-2026",
        sex: "Female",
        rash_onset_date: null,
        zip: null,
        age_years: null,
        county: null,
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Bronx 2026-03",
        case_id: "8-2026",
        sex: "Male",
        rash_onset_date: null,
        zip: null,
        age_years: null,
        county: null,
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Kings 2026-03",
        case_id: "K1",
        sex: "Male",
        rash_onset_date: "2026-03-02",
        zip: "00501",
        age_years: 2,
        county: "Kings",
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Kings 2026-03",
        case_id: "K2",
        sex: "Female",
        rash_onset_date: null,
        zip: "10451",
        age_years: 0.5,
        county: "Kings",
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Kings O'Brien $& --",
        case_id: "K3",
        sex: "Unknown",
        rash_onset_date: "2026-04-01",
        zip: "1234567",
        age_years: 1.5,
        county: "Kings",
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Queens 2026-03",
        case_id: "Q1",
        sex: "Male",
        rash_onset_date: "2026-03-05",
        zip: "11368",
        age_years: null,
        county: "Queens",
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
      {
        source_dataset: "Queens 2026-03",
        case_id: "Q2",
        sex: "Other",
        rash_onset_date: "2026-03-06",
        zip: "11101",
        age_years: null,
        county: "Queens",
        outbreak_associated: null,
      },
    ]);
  });

  it("types every column as the crosswalk says", async () => {
    const { types } = await _readCombined(_compile("labels").sql);

    expect(types).toEqual({
      source_dataset: "VARCHAR",
      case_id: "VARCHAR",
      sex: "VARCHAR",
      rash_onset_date: "DATE",
      zip: "VARCHAR",
      age_years: "DOUBLE",
      county: "VARCHAR",
      outbreak_associated: "BOOLEAN",
    });
  });

  it("reconciles every coding to the primary codes in codes mode, emptying a code with no counterpart", async () => {
    const { rows, types } = await _readCombined(_compile("codes").sql);

    expect(
      rows.map((row) => {
        return [row.case_id, row.sex];
      }),
    ).toEqual([
      ["7-2026", "2"],
      ["8-2026", "1"],
      ["K1", "1"],
      ["K2", "2"],
      ["K3", "9"],
      ["Q1", "1"],
      ["Q2", null],
    ]);
    expect(types.sex).toBe("BIGINT");
  });
});
```

### Task 12: The draft shape, Combine checks, and the browser compile

Three browser modules the crosswalk view builds on. `CrosswalkDraft.types.ts` is the shape the reducer edits and saves whole, exactly as the contract gives it; Task 15 writes the `CrosswalkDraft` module and namespace beside it, so this task's code imports `CrosswalkDraftT` and `CrosswalkDraftLayout` from the types file directly.

`validateCombineExpression` checks a Combine expression the way the combined dataset runs it: every placeholder must be one of the layout's columns, ignoring case, and the expression with its placeholders quoted (`CrosswalkSql.toExpressionSql`) must pass `assertSingleSqlExpression`, which refuses a second expression, an alias, a clause or subquery, `;` and comments, and file-reading functions.

`compileCrosswalk` is the step-3 compile. It leaves out skipped layouts, layouts with no dataset (the reference included), and datasets whose current columns no longer match their layout's key (`columns_changed`, compared with `CrosswalkLayout.hasColumnsChanged`); it uses every other fill, confirmed or suggested, and counts the datasets of layouts not yet `mapped` (`unconfirmed`) and of skipped layouts (`skipped`). It blocks on an invalid Combine expression and when nothing is left to combine, reports a fill whose code list is gone (`missing_code_list`; `CrosswalkSql` then passes its values through), and builds one reference binding per governed column whose entry still has a primary list, holding labels (`encode`) in labels mode and codes (`decode`) in codes mode. The code lists come from `entriesById`, each entry's first list being its primary one.

```ts
import type { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import type { CrosswalkColumn } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkColumn/CrosswalkColumn";
import type { CrosswalkDataset } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkDataset/CrosswalkDataset";
import type { CrosswalkLayout } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkLayout/CrosswalkLayout";
import type { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import type { DataDictionaryEntry } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryEntry/DataDictionaryEntry";
import type { AvaDataType } from "$/models/datasets/AvaDataType/AvaDataType";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

/** One column of the combined dataset while the crosswalk is edited. */
export type CrosswalkDraftColumn = {
  id: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
  name: string;
  position: number;
  dataType: AvaDataType.T;
  entryId: DataDictionaryEntry.Id | undefined;
};

/** One layout while the crosswalk is edited, with the datasets it maps. */
export type CrosswalkDraftLayout = {
  id: CrosswalkLayout.Id;
  /** `CrosswalkLayout.buildLayoutKey` of its column names */
  key: string;
  signature: string;
  columnNames: readonly string[];
  isReference: boolean;
  status: CrosswalkLayout.Status;
  /** Sorted by dataset name. */
  datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[];
};

/** How one column is filled for one layout while the crosswalk is edited. */
export type CrosswalkDraftMapping = {
  id: CrosswalkMapping.Id;
  fill: CrosswalkMapping.Fill;
  status: CrosswalkMapping.Status;
  confidence: number | undefined;
  reason: CrosswalkMapping.Reason | undefined;
};

/** A whole crosswalk as the browser edits it, saved whole. */
export type CrosswalkDraftT = {
  crosswalkId: Crosswalk.Id;
  /** False until the crosswalk row exists. */
  isSaved: boolean;
  name: string;
  description: string | undefined;
  codesOutputAs: Crosswalk.CodesOutput;
  addsSourceColumn: boolean;
  outputDatasetId: Dataset.Id | undefined;
  /** In position order, positions 0..n-1. */
  columns: readonly CrosswalkDraftColumn[];
  /** The reference layout first, then by first dataset name. */
  layouts: readonly CrosswalkDraftLayout[];
  /** By layout id, then column id. A missing entry means no fill yet. */
  mappings: Readonly<
    Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, CrosswalkDraftMapping>>>
  >;
};

/** What the crosswalk's five tables hold, read through their clients. */
export type CrosswalkContents = {
  crosswalk: Crosswalk.T;
  columns: readonly CrosswalkColumn.T[];
  layouts: readonly CrosswalkLayout.T[];
  datasets: readonly CrosswalkDataset.T[];
  mappings: readonly CrosswalkMapping.T[];
};
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { validateCombineExpression } from "@/lib/crosswalks/validateCombineExpression/validateCombineExpression";

const COLUMN_NAMES = ["Case No", "first_name", "last_name", "Year"];

describe("validateCombineExpression", () => {
  it("accepts one expression over the layout's columns, matched ignoring case", () => {
    expect(
      validateCombineExpression({
        sql: "concat({case no}, '-', {YEAR})",
        columnNames: COLUMN_NAMES,
      }),
    ).toEqual({ isValid: true });
  });

  it("refuses an empty expression", () => {
    expect(
      validateCombineExpression({ sql: "   ", columnNames: COLUMN_NAMES }),
    ).toEqual({ isValid: false, reason: "empty" });
  });

  it("names the first placeholder that is not one of the layout's columns", () => {
    expect(
      validateCombineExpression({
        sql: "concat({first_name}, ' ', {surname}, {nickname})",
        columnNames: COLUMN_NAMES,
      }),
    ).toEqual({
      isValid: false,
      reason: "unknown_column",
      columnName: "surname",
    });
  });

  it.each([
    ["two expressions", "{first_name}, {last_name}"],
    ["a subquery", "(SELECT 1)"],
    ["a statement break", "{first_name}; DROP TABLE x"],
    ["a file read", "read_csv('/etc/passwd')"],
    ["an alias", "{first_name} AS name"],
  ])("refuses %s as invalid SQL", (_label, sql) => {
    expect(
      validateCombineExpression({ sql, columnNames: COLUMN_NAMES }),
    ).toEqual({ isValid: false, reason: "invalid_sql" });
  });
});
```

```ts
    kind: "column",
    sourceColumn,
    convert: undefined,
    codeListId,
    holdsLabels: false,
  };
}

function _draft(changes: Partial<CrosswalkDraftT> = {}): CrosswalkDraftT {
  return {
    crosswalkId: "crosswalk-1" as Crosswalk.Id,
    isSaved: true,
    name: "Measles line lists",
    description: undefined,
    codesOutputAs: "labels",
    addsSourceColumn: true,
    outputDatasetId: undefined,
    columns: [
      {
        id: CASE_ID,
        name: "case_id",
        position: 0,
        dataType: "varchar",
        entryId: undefined,
      },
      {
        id: SEX,
        name: "sex",
        position: 1,
        dataType: "varchar",
        entryId: ENTRY_SEX.entryId,
      },
    ],
    layouts: [
      _layout("layout-kings", KINGS_COLUMNS, ["dataset-k1", "dataset-k2"], {
        isReference: true,
        status: "mapped",
      }),
      _layout("layout-queens", QUEENS_COLUMNS, ["dataset-q1"]),
    ],
    mappings: {
      "layout-kings": {
        [CASE_ID]: _mapping(_columnFill("CaseNo")),
        [SEX]: _mapping(_columnFill("GENDER", SEX_129.id)),
      },
      "layout-queens": {
        [CASE_ID]: _mapping(_columnFill("case_id"), "suggested"),
        [SEX]: _mapping(_columnFill("sex", SEX_MFU.id), "suggested"),
      },
    },
    ...changes,
  };
}

function _compile(draft: CrosswalkDraftT): ReturnType<typeof compileCrosswalk> {
  return compileCrosswalk({
    draft,
    datasetsById: DATASETS_BY_ID,
    entriesById: ENTRIES_BY_ID,
  });
}

describe("compileCrosswalk", () => {
  it("compiles every layout's datasets with the source column first", () => {
    const result = _compile(_draft());

    expect(result.status).toBe("ready");
    if (result.status !== "ready") {
      return;
    }
    expect(result.includedDatasetIds).toEqual([
      "dataset-k1",
      "dataset-k2",
      "dataset-q1",
    ]);
    expect(result.columns).toEqual([
      { name: "source_dataset", dataType: "varchar" },
      { name: "case_id", dataType: "varchar" },
      { name: "sex", dataType: "varchar" },
    ]);
    expect(result.sql).toContain(`'Kings 2026-04' AS "__ava_source_dataset"`);
  });

  it("binds each governed column to its entry's primary list, holding labels in labels mode", () => {
    const result = _compile(_draft());

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.bindings).toEqual([
      {
        columnName: "sex",
        dictionaryId: ENTRY_SEX.dictionaryId,
        entryId: ENTRY_SEX.entryId,
        codeListId: SEX_129.id,
        direction: "encode",
      },
    ]);
  });

  it("binds governed columns as holding codes in codes mode", () => {
    const result = _compile(_draft({ codesOutputAs: "codes" }));

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.bindings[0]?.direction).toBe(
      "decode",
    );
  });

  it("binds nothing for a column whose entry is gone", () => {
    const result = compileCrosswalk({
      draft: _draft(),
      datasetsById: DATASETS_BY_ID,
      entriesById: new Map(),
    });

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.bindings).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("fingerprints every code list the SQL embedded", () => {
    const result = _compile(_draft());

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.compiledCodeLists).toEqual([
      {
        codeListId: SEX_129.id,
        fingerprint: CrosswalkSql.getCodeListFingerprint(SEX_129.pairs),
      },
      {
        codeListId: SEX_MFU.id,
        fingerprint: CrosswalkSql.getCodeListFingerprint(SEX_MFU.pairs),
      },
    ]);
  });

  it("counts the datasets of layouts not yet confirmed", () => {
    expect(_compile(_draft()).problems).toEqual([
      { kind: "unconfirmed", datasetCount: 1 },
    ]);
  });

  it("leaves out and counts a skipped layout's datasets", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      layouts: [draft.layouts[0]!, { ...draft.layouts[1]!, status: "skipped" }],
    });

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.includedDatasetIds).toEqual([
      "dataset-k1",
      "dataset-k2",
    ]);
    expect(result.problems).toEqual([{ kind: "skipped", datasetCount: 1 }]);
  });

  it("leaves out a dataset whose columns changed since it was mapped", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      layouts: [
        {
          ...draft.layouts[0]!,
          datasetIds: ["dataset-b1", "dataset-k1"] as Dataset.Id[],
        },
        draft.layouts[1]!,
      ],
    });

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.includedDatasetIds).toEqual([
      "dataset-k1",
      "dataset-q1",
    ]);
    expect(result.problems).toContainEqual({
      kind: "columns_changed",
      datasetId: "dataset-b1",
      datasetName: "Bronx 2026-03",
    });
  });

  it("leaves out a layout with no dataset, even the reference", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      layouts: [{ ...draft.layouts[0]!, datasetIds: [] }, draft.layouts[1]!],
    });

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.includedDatasetIds).toEqual([
      "dataset-q1",
    ]);
  });

  it("blocks on a Combine expression naming a column the layout lacks", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      mappings: {
        ...draft.mappings,
        "layout-queens": {
          [CASE_ID]: _mapping({ kind: "expression", sql: "upper({CaseNo})" }),
        },
      },
    });

    expect(result).toEqual({
      status: "blocked",
      problems: [
        {
          kind: "invalid_expression",
          layoutId: "layout-queens",
          columnId: CASE_ID,
        },
        { kind: "unconfirmed", datasetCount: 1 },
      ],
    });
  });

  it("compiles a Combine expression over the layout's own columns", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      mappings: {
        ...draft.mappings,
        "layout-queens": {
          [CASE_ID]: _mapping({
            kind: "expression",
            sql: "upper({Full_Name})",
          }),
        },
      },
    });

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.sql).toContain(
      `TRY_CAST((upper("Full_Name")) AS VARCHAR) AS "case_id"`,
    );
  });

  it("reports a fill whose code list is gone, and lets its values pass through", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      mappings: {
        ...draft.mappings,
        "layout-queens": {
          [SEX]: _mapping(
            _columnFill("sex", "list-gone" as DataDictionaryCodeList.Id),
          ),
        },
      },
    });

    expect(result.status).toBe("ready");
    expect(result.problems).toContainEqual({
      kind: "missing_code_list",
      layoutId: "layout-queens",
      columnId: SEX,
    });
    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.sql).toContain(
      `CAST("sex" AS VARCHAR) AS "sex"`,
    );
  });

  it("blocks when every layout is skipped", () => {
    const draft = _draft();
    const result = _compile({
      ...draft,
      layouts: draft.layouts.map((layout) => {
        return { ...layout, status: "skipped" as const };
      }),
    });

    expect(result).toEqual({
      status: "blocked",
      problems: [
        { kind: "skipped", datasetCount: 3 },
        { kind: "nothing_to_combine" },
      ],
    });
  });

  it("drops the source column when the crosswalk adds none", () => {
    const result = _compile(_draft({ addsSourceColumn: false }));

    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.columns[0]?.name).toBe(
      "case_id",
    );
    expect(result.status === "ready" && result.sql).not.toContain(
      "source_dataset",
    );
  });
});
```

```ts
import { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import { CrosswalkSql } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkSql/CrosswalkSql";
import { assertSingleSqlExpression } from "@/lib/plugins/derivedColumns/assertSingleSqlExpression/assertSingleSqlExpression";

/** Whether a Combine expression can fill a column, and if not, why not. */
export type CombineExpressionCheck =
  | { isValid: true }
  | {
      isValid: false;
      reason: "empty" | "unknown_column" | "invalid_sql";
      columnName?: string;
    };

/**
 * Whether a Combine expression names only the layout's columns, ignoring
 * case, and is one SQL expression once its placeholders are quoted, the
 * way the combined dataset runs it. Use it to explain a bad expression
 * while it is typed, and to block a combine that would run one.
 */
export function validateCombineExpression(
  options: Readonly<{ sql: string; columnNames: readonly string[] }>,
): CombineExpressionCheck {
  if (options.sql.trim() === "") {
    return { isValid: false, reason: "empty" };
  }
  const knownNames = new Set(
    options.columnNames.map((columnName) => {
      return columnName.trim().toLowerCase();
    }),
  );
  const unknownName = CrosswalkMapping.getCombineColumnNames(options.sql).find(
    (columnName) => {
      return !knownNames.has(columnName.toLowerCase());
    },
  );
  if (unknownName !== undefined) {
    return {
      isValid: false,
      reason: "unknown_column",
      columnName: unknownName,
    };
  }
  try {
    assertSingleSqlExpression(CrosswalkSql.toExpressionSql(options.sql));
  } catch {
    return { isValid: false, reason: "invalid_sql" };
  }
  return { isValid: true };
}
```

`src/lib/crosswalks/compileCrosswalk/compileCrosswalk.ts`:

```ts
import { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import { CrosswalkLayout } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkLayout/CrosswalkLayout";
import { CrosswalkSql } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkSql/CrosswalkSql";
import { validateCombineExpression } from "@/lib/crosswalks/validateCombineExpression/validateCombineExpression";
import type { CrosswalkColumn } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkColumn/CrosswalkColumn";
import type { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import type { DataDictionaryCodeList } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryCodeList/DataDictionaryCodeList";
import type { DictionaryMatch } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DictionaryMatch/DictionaryMatch";
import type { AvaDataType } from "$/models/datasets/AvaDataType/AvaDataType";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";
import type {
  CrosswalkDraftLayout,
  CrosswalkDraftT,
} from "@/lib/crosswalks/CrosswalkDraft/CrosswalkDraft.types";

/** Something step 3 says about the combined dataset before it is saved. */
export type CrosswalkProblem =
  /** The dataset is left out: its columns changed since it was mapped. */
  | { kind: "columns_changed"; datasetId: Dataset.Id; datasetName: string }
  /** Blocks: a Combine expression the combined dataset cannot run. */
  | {
      kind: "invalid_expression";
      layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id;
      columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
    }
  /** The fill's code list is gone, so its values pass through unchanged. */
  | {
      kind: "missing_code_list";
      layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id;
      columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id;
    }
  /** Blocks: no layout has a dataset to combine. */
  | { kind: "nothing_to_combine" }
  | { kind: "unconfirmed"; datasetCount: number }
  | { kind: "skipped"; datasetCount: number };

/** The combined dataset ready to save, or why it cannot be. */
export type CompileCrosswalkResult =
  | {
      status: "ready";
      sql: string;
      columns: Array<{ name: string; dataType: AvaDataType.T }>;
      bindings: Crosswalk.CombinePayload["bindings"];
      compiledCodeLists: Crosswalk.CompiledCodeList[];
      includedDatasetIds: Dataset.Id[];
      problems: CrosswalkProblem[];
    }
  | { status: "blocked"; problems: CrosswalkProblem[] };

type CompileOptions = Readonly<{
  draft: CrosswalkDraftT;
  datasetsById: ReadonlyMap<string, CrosswalkLayout.Dataset>;
  entriesById: ReadonlyMap<string, DictionaryMatch.Entry>;
}>;

type CodeListsById = ReadonlyMap<
  string,
  { pairs: readonly DataDictionaryCodeList.Pair[] }
>;

/** One layout's part of the compile: what it adds, and what it reports. */
type LayoutPart = {
  sqlLayout: CrosswalkSql.Layout | undefined;
  problems: CrosswalkProblem[];
  unconfirmedCount: number;
};

function _getCodeListsById(
  entriesById: CompileOptions["entriesById"],
): CodeListsById {
  return new Map(
    [...entriesById.values()].flatMap((entry) => {
      return entry.codeLists.map((codeList) => {
        return [codeList.id as string, { pairs: codeList.pairs }] as const;
      });
    }),
  );
}

/** The layout's datasets whose columns still match it, and the others. */
function _splitDatasets(
  layout: CrosswalkDraftLayout,
  datasetsById: CompileOptions["datasetsById"],
): { included: CrosswalkLayout.Dataset[]; problems: CrosswalkProblem[] } {
  const datasets = layout.datasetIds.flatMap((datasetId) => {
    const dataset = datasetsById.get(datasetId);
    return dataset ? [dataset] : [];
  });
  const changed = datasets.filter((dataset) => {
    return CrosswalkLayout.hasColumnsChanged({
      layoutKey: layout.key,
      currentColumnNames: dataset.columns.map((column) => {
        return column.name;
      }),
    });
  });
  return {
    included: datasets.filter((dataset) => {
      return !changed.includes(dataset);
    }),
    problems: changed.map((dataset) => {
      return {
        kind: "columns_changed",
        datasetId: dataset.id,
        datasetName: dataset.name,
      };
    }),
  };
}

function _getFillProblem(
  layout: CrosswalkDraftLayout,
  columnId: CrosswalkColumn.Id,
  fill: CrosswalkMapping.Fill,
  codeListsById: CodeListsById,
): CrosswalkProblem | undefined {
  if (
    fill.kind === "expression" &&
    !validateCombineExpression({
      sql: fill.sql,
      columnNames: layout.columnNames,
    }).isValid
  ) {
    return { kind: "invalid_expression", layoutId: layout.id, columnId };
  }
  if (
    fill.kind === "column" &&
    fill.codeListId !== undefined &&
    !codeListsById.has(fill.codeListId)
  ) {
    return { kind: "missing_code_list", layoutId: layout.id, columnId };
  }
  return undefined;
}

function _toLayoutPart(
  layout: CrosswalkDraftLayout,
  options: CompileOptions,
  codeListsById: CodeListsById,
): LayoutPart {
  const { included, problems } = _splitDatasets(layout, options.datasetsById);
  if (included.length === 0) {
    return { sqlLayout: undefined, problems, unconfirmedCount: 0 };
  }
  const columnIds = new Set<string>(
    options.draft.columns.map((column) => {
      return column.id;
    }),
  );
  const fills = Object.entries(options.draft.mappings[layout.id] ?? {}).filter(
    ([columnId]) => {
      return columnIds.has(columnId);
    },
  );
  const fillProblems = fills.flatMap(([columnId, mapping]) => {
    const problem = _getFillProblem(
      layout,
      columnId as CrosswalkColumn.Id,
      mapping.fill,
      codeListsById,
    );
    return problem ? [problem] : [];
  });
  return {
    sqlLayout: {
      layoutId: layout.id,
      datasets: included.map((dataset) => {
        return { id: dataset.id, name: dataset.name };
      }),
      fillsByColumnId: new Map(
        fills.map(([columnId, mapping]) => {
          return [columnId, mapping.fill] as const;
        }),
      ),
    },
    problems: [...problems, ...fillProblems],
    unconfirmedCount: layout.status === "mapped" ? 0 : included.length,
  };
}

function _getBindings(
  draft: CrosswalkDraftT,
  entriesById: CompileOptions["entriesById"],
): Crosswalk.CombinePayload["bindings"] {
  return draft.columns.flatMap((column) => {
    const entry =
      column.entryId === undefined
        ? undefined
        : entriesById.get(column.entryId);
    const primaryList = entry?.codeLists[0];
    if (!entry || !primaryList) {
      return [];
    }
    return [
      {
        columnName: column.name,
        dictionaryId: entry.dictionaryId,
        entryId: entry.entryId,
        codeListId: primaryList.id,
        direction: draft.codesOutputAs === "labels" ? "encode" : "decode",
      },
    ];
  });
}

function _getPrimaryCodeListIdByEntryId(
  entriesById: CompileOptions["entriesById"],
): Map<string, string> {
  return new Map(
    [...entriesById.values()].flatMap((entry) => {
      const primaryList = entry.codeLists[0];
      return primaryList
        ? [[entry.entryId as string, primaryList.id as string] as const]
        : [];
    }),
  );
}

function _countProblems(
  draft: CrosswalkDraftT,
  parts: readonly LayoutPart[],
): CrosswalkProblem[] {
  const unconfirmedCount = parts.reduce((sum, part) => {
    return sum + part.unconfirmedCount;
  }, 0);
  const skippedCount = draft.layouts
    .filter((layout) => {
      return layout.status === "skipped";
    })
    .reduce((sum, layout) => {
      return sum + layout.datasetIds.length;
    }, 0);
  return [
    ...(unconfirmedCount > 0
      ? [{ kind: "unconfirmed" as const, datasetCount: unconfirmedCount }]
      : []),
    ...(skippedCount > 0
      ? [{ kind: "skipped" as const, datasetCount: skippedCount }]
      : []),
  ];
}

function _compileSql(
  options: CompileOptions,
  sqlLayouts: readonly CrosswalkSql.Layout[],
  codeListsById: CodeListsById,
): CrosswalkSql.Output | undefined {
  try {
    return CrosswalkSql.compile({
      codesOutputAs: options.draft.codesOutputAs,
      sourceColumnName: options.draft.addsSourceColumn
        ? Crosswalk.SOURCE_COLUMN_NAME
        : undefined,
      columns: options.draft.columns,
      layouts: sqlLayouts,
      codeListsById,
      primaryCodeListIdByEntryId: _getPrimaryCodeListIdByEntryId(
        options.entriesById,
      ),
    });
  } catch (error) {
    if (
      error instanceof Error &&
      error.message === "crosswalk-nothing-to-combine"
    ) {
      return undefined;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

/** Each layout's part of the SQL, and every problem the layouts report. */
function _compileLayouts(
  options: CompileOptions,
  codeListsById: CodeListsById,
): { sqlLayouts: CrosswalkSql.Layout[]; problems: CrosswalkProblem[] } {
  const parts = options.draft.layouts
    .filter((layout) => {
      return layout.status !== "skipped";
    })
    .map((layout) => {
      return _toLayoutPart(layout, options, codeListsById);
    });
  return {
    sqlLayouts: parts.flatMap((part) => {
      return part.sqlLayout ? [part.sqlLayout] : [];
    }),
    problems: [
      ...parts.flatMap((part) => {
        return part.problems;
      }),
      ..._countProblems(options.draft, parts),
    ],
  };
}

/** A fingerprint of each code list the SQL embedded, for the stale banner. */
function _getCompiledCodeLists(
  usedCodeListIds: readonly string[],
  codeListsById: CodeListsById,
): Crosswalk.CompiledCodeList[] {
  return usedCodeListIds.flatMap((codeListId) => {
    const codeList = codeListsById.get(codeListId);
    return codeList
      ? [
          {
            codeListId: codeListId as DataDictionaryCodeList.Id,
            fingerprint: CrosswalkSql.getCodeListFingerprint(codeList.pairs),
          },
        ]
      : [];
  });
}

/**
 * Compiles a crosswalk draft into its combined dataset, ready for
 * `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset`. Skipped layouts, layouts with no
 * dataset, and datasets whose columns changed since they were mapped are
 * left out; every other fill is used, confirmed or not. Blocks on an
 * invalid Combine expression or when nothing is left to combine. Use it
 * for the combine step's preview, problems, and save.
 */
export function compileCrosswalk(
  options: CompileOptions,
): CompileCrosswalkResult {
  const codeListsById = _getCodeListsById(options.entriesById);
  const { sqlLayouts, problems } = _compileLayouts(options, codeListsById);
  const output = _compileSql(options, sqlLayouts, codeListsById);
  if (output === undefined) {
    return {
      status: "blocked",
      problems: [...problems, { kind: "nothing_to_combine" }],
    };
  }
  if (
    problems.some((problem) => {
      return problem.kind === "invalid_expression";
    })
  ) {
    return { status: "blocked", problems };
  }
  return {
    status: "ready",
    sql: output.sql,
    columns: output.columns,
    bindings: _getBindings(options.draft, options.entriesById),
    compiledCodeLists: _getCompiledCodeLists(
      output.usedCodeListIds,
      codeListsById,
    ),
    includedDatasetIds: sqlLayouts.flatMap((layout) => {
      return layout.datasets.map((dataset) => {
        return dataset.id;
      });
    }),
    problems,
  };
}
```

### Task 13: The crosswalk clients

Five clients, one per crosswalk table, built exactly like the dictionary clients: `createRdbCrudClient` wrapped in `createUsableServiceClient`. Only `CrosswalkClient` writes. Besides the generated CRUD (`insert` creates the row a new crosswalk saves into, `update` and `delete` act on the row), it gains the two RPC mutations from the contract. Everything under the crosswalk (columns, layouts, memberships, mappings) is written whole through `saveContents`, never row by row, so the four child clients are read-only, like `DataDictionaryEntryClient`.

The mutations map the model-shaped payloads to the RPCs' snake_case jsonb with module-private `_...ToRpcArg` helpers, as `DataDictionaryClient` does: every `undefined` becomes `null`, readonly arrays are copied into plain arrays (the generated `Json` type does not accept a readonly array), and a fill goes through `CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson`, so the stored fill is the versioned snake_case shape the parser reads back. A refusal rejects with the PostgREST error; callers read its hint with `Crosswalk.toSaveErrorHint` or `Crosswalk.toCombineErrorHint` (Task 16's `useCrosswalkErrorMessage`).

```ts
import type { DataDictionary } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionary/DataDictionary";
import type { DataDictionaryCodeList } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryCodeList/DataDictionaryCodeList";

const { CrosswalkClient } = await import("./CrosswalkClient");
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `src/clients/crosswalks/CrosswalkClient.ts`:**

```ts
import { CrosswalkParsers } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import { createRdbCrudClient } from "$/RdbCrudClient/createRdbCrudClient";
import { createUsableServiceClient } from "@/utils/createUsableServiceClient";
import type { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

type SavePayload = Crosswalk.SavePayload;
type CombinePayload = Crosswalk.CombinePayload;

function _settingsToRpcArg(settings: SavePayload["settings"]) {
  return {
    name: settings.name,
    description: settings.description ?? null,
    codes_output_as: settings.codesOutputAs,
    adds_source_column: settings.addsSourceColumn,
  };
}

function _columnToRpcArg(column: SavePayload["columns"][number]) {
  return {
    id: column.id,
    name: column.name,
    position: column.position,
    data_type: column.dataType,
    entry_id: column.entryId ?? null,
  };
}

function _layoutToRpcArg(layout: SavePayload["layouts"][number]) {
  return {
    id: layout.id,
    signature: layout.signature,
    column_names: [...layout.columnNames],
    is_reference: layout.isReference,
    status: layout.status,
  };
}

function _mappingToRpcArg(mapping: SavePayload["mappings"][number]) {
  return {
    id: mapping.id,
    layout_id: mapping.layoutId,
    column_id: mapping.columnId,
    fill: CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson(mapping.fill),
    status: mapping.status,
    confidence: mapping.confidence ?? null,
    reason: mapping.reason ?? null,
  };
}

function _toSaveRpcArgs(payload: SavePayload) {
  return {
    p_crosswalk_id: payload.crosswalkId,
    p_settings: _settingsToRpcArg(payload.settings),
    p_columns: payload.columns.map(_columnToRpcArg),
    p_layouts: payload.layouts.map(_layoutToRpcArg),
    p_datasets: payload.datasets.map((membership) => {
      return {
        dataset_id: membership.datasetId,
        layout_id: membership.layoutId,
      };
    }),
    p_mappings: payload.mappings.map(_mappingToRpcArg),
  };
}

function _toCombineRpcArgs(payload: CombinePayload) {
  return {
    p_crosswalk_id: payload.crosswalkId,
    p_dataset_id: payload.datasetId,
    p_dataset_name: payload.datasetName,
    p_raw_sql: payload.rawSql,
    p_columns: payload.columns.map((column) => {
      return { name: column.name, data_type: column.dataType };
    }),
    p_bindings: payload.bindings.map((binding) => {
      return {
        column_name: binding.columnName,
        dictionary_id: binding.dictionaryId,
        entry_id: binding.entryId,
        code_list_id: binding.codeListId,
        direction: binding.direction,
      };
    }),
    p_compiled_code_lists: payload.compiledCodeLists.map((list) => {
      return { code_list_id: list.codeListId, fingerprint: list.fingerprint };
    }),
  };
}

/**
 * Reads, creates, renames, and deletes crosswalks. A crosswalk's columns,
 * layouts, memberships, and mappings are saved whole through
 * `saveContents`, never row by row, and its combined dataset is created or
 * updated through `saveCombinedDataset`.
 */
export const CrosswalkClient = createUsableServiceClient(
  createRdbCrudClient({
    modelName: "Crosswalk",
    tableName: "crosswalks",
    dbTablePrimaryKey: "id",
    parsers: CrosswalkParsers,
    mutations: ({ clientLogger, dbClient }) => {
      return {
        /**
         * Replaces one crosswalk's settings, columns, layouts, memberships,
         * and mappings in one transaction. A refusal rejects with the RPC's
         * `hint`; read it with `Crosswalk.toSaveErrorHint`.
         */
        saveContents: async (payload: SavePayload): Promise<void> => {
          clientLogger.appendName("saveContents").log("Saving crosswalk", {
            crosswalkId: payload.crosswalkId,
            layoutCount: payload.layouts.length,
            mappingCount: payload.mappings.length,
          });
          await dbClient
            .rpc("rpc_crosswalks__save", _toSaveRpcArgs(payload))
            .throwOnError();
        },

        /**
         * Creates the crosswalk's combined dataset, or updates it when the
         * crosswalk already has one, and returns its id. A refusal rejects
         * with the RPC's `hint`; read it with `Crosswalk.toCombineErrorHint`.
         */
        saveCombinedDataset: async (
          payload: CombinePayload,
        ): Promise<Dataset.Id> => {
          clientLogger
            .appendName("saveCombinedDataset")
            .log("Saving combined dataset", {
              crosswalkId: payload.crosswalkId,
              datasetId: payload.datasetId,
              columnCount: payload.columns.length,
            });
          const { data } = await dbClient
            .rpc(
              "rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset",
              _toCombineRpcArgs(payload),
            )
            .throwOnError();
          return data as Dataset.Id;
        },
      };
    },
  }),
  {
    mutationFns: ["saveContents", "saveCombinedDataset"],
  },
);
```

`CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson` returns Task 7's `StoredCrosswalkFill` (exported from `CrosswalkMapping.ts`), a plain object type whose every field is a value or `| null`, so it is assignable to the generated `Json`. If `pnpm exec tsc -b --force --noEmit` (Step 6) still rejects an argument because the generated RPC types declare it `Json` and a value is not assignable, cast that one argument with `as Json` (`import type { Json } from "$/types/database.types";`, the path `shared/types/database.types.ts` exports it from) rather than loosening the payload types. Check the exact export first with `grep -n "export type Json" shared/types/database.types.ts`.

### Task 14: Permission, routes, links, the Crosswalks list group, and New crosswalk

Wires crosswalks into Data Sources before the view exists: the `data_sources__can_edit_crosswalks` permission (Data Sources editors and admins, matching the RLS on `crosswalks`), the two routes, their `AppLinks`, the list pane collapsing on both crosswalk routes, a **Crosswalks** group in the list, and **New crosswalk** in the toolbar.

Crosswalks show in the list only to someone who can edit them. A Data Sources viewer can read the rows (RLS allows it), but every crosswalk surface is an editor's task view, so a viewer would get a list entry that opens onto "You can't edit crosswalks". The lists hook therefore does not fetch crosswalks at all without the permission (`enabled: false`), and the navbar renders whatever it is given. The hook moves out of `DataManagerApp.tsx` into its own file so it can be tested; `DataManagerApp` keeps calling it.

The routes import `CrosswalkView`, which Task 16 builds. This task creates a placeholder `CV/CrosswalkView.tsx` that renders only a status `Loader`, so the route files compile and the route tree regenerates. Task 16 replaces it whole. The `$crosswalkId` route validates `step` and `layoutId` with zod the way `$datasetId_.apply-dictionaries.tsx` validates `dictionaryId`; the view reads them itself (Task 16's `useCrosswalkFlow`), so the route does not pass them down. A bad value falls back to `undefined` through `.catch(undefined)` instead of failing the route.

`search` is not part of the `AppLink` type. The record's functions return inferred types that only need to be assignable to `AppLink`, so the extra field type-checks, and callers that navigate pass it on explicitly (`navigate({ to: link.to, params: link.params, search: link.search })`). Callers that render a nav row take only `to` and `params`, as `DatasetNavbar` already does.

```tsx
import { createFileRoute } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { z } from "zod";
import { CrosswalkView } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/CrosswalkView";
import type { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

export const Route = createFileRoute(
  "/_auth/$workspaceSlug/data-manager/crosswalks/$crosswalkId",
)({
  component: RouteComponent,
  // The view reads the step and layout itself, so moving between steps
  // changes only the search and never remounts the view.
  validateSearch: z.object({
    step: z.enum(["datasets", "map", "combine"]).optional().catch(undefined),
    layoutId: z.uuid().optional().catch(undefined),
  }),
});

function RouteComponent(): ReactNode {
  const { crosswalkId } = Route.useParams();
  // The router's typing drops the id's brand, so restore it. A new key
  // starts the view over for another crosswalk.
  return (
    <CrosswalkView key={crosswalkId} crosswalkId={crosswalkId as Crosswalk.Id} />
  );
}
```

TanStack Router ranks the static `crosswalks/new` above the dynamic `crosswalks/$crosswalkId`, so `/crosswalks/new` never opens as a crosswalk with the id `new`.

```ts
import { where } from "@avandar/utils";
import { CrosswalkClient } from "@/clients/crosswalks/CrosswalkClient";
import { DataDictionaryClient } from "@/clients/dataDictionaries/DataDictionaryClient/DataDictionaryClient";
import { DatasetClient } from "@/clients/datasets/DatasetClient/DatasetClient";
import { useHasPermission } from "@/hooks/permissions/useHasPermission/useHasPermission";
import { useCurrentWorkspace } from "@/hooks/workspaces/useCurrentWorkspace";
import type { Crosswalk } from "$/models/crosswalks/Crosswalk/Crosswalk";
import type { DataDictionary } from "$/models/dataDictionaries/DataDictionary/DataDictionary";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

/** What the Data Sources list shows. */
export type DataManagerLists = {
  datasets: Dataset.T[];
  dictionaries: DataDictionary.T[];
  /** Empty for someone who cannot edit crosswalks. */
  crosswalks: Crosswalk.T[];
  isLoading: boolean;
};

/**
 * The workspace's datasets, dictionaries, and crosswalks that the Data
 * Sources list shows. Crosswalks are read only for someone who can edit
 * them: every crosswalk opens onto an editor's task, so listing one to a
 * viewer would only lead to a no-access notice.
 */
export function useDataManagerLists(): DataManagerLists {
  const workspace = useCurrentWorkspace();
  const canEditCrosswalks = useHasPermission(
    "data_sources__can_edit_crosswalks",
  );
  const [datasets, isLoadingDatasets] = DatasetClient.useGetAll(
    where("workspace_id", "eq", workspace.id),
  );
  const [dictionaries, isLoadingDictionaries] = DataDictionaryClient.useGetAll(
    where("workspace_id", "eq", workspace.id),
  );
  const [crosswalks, isLoadingCrosswalks] = CrosswalkClient.useGetAll({
    ...where("workspace_id", "eq", workspace.id),
    useQueryOptions: { enabled: canEditCrosswalks },
  });
  return {
    datasets: datasets ?? [],
    dictionaries: dictionaries ?? [],
    crosswalks: canEditCrosswalks ? (crosswalks ?? []) : [],
    isLoading: isLoadingDatasets || isLoadingDictionaries || isLoadingCrosswalks,
  };
}
```

A disabled query reports `isLoading` false (TanStack Query v5: `isLoading` is `isPending && isFetching`), so a viewer's list never waits on it.

```tsx
function makeCrosswalkLink(options: {
  workspaceSlug: string;
  crosswalk: Crosswalk.T;
}): NavLinkProps & { key: string } {
  const { workspaceSlug, crosswalk } = options;
  // Destination only, for the same reasons as `makeDatasetLink`.
  const { to, params } = AppLinks.dataManagerCrosswalkView({
    workspaceSlug,
    crosswalkId: crosswalk.id,
    crosswalkName: crosswalk.name,
  });
  return {
    key: crosswalk.id,
    to,
    params,
    className: css.datasetNavbarLink,
    leftSection: <IconArrowMerge size={16} stroke={1.6} aria-hidden />,
    label: <DatasetNavbarName name={crosswalk.name} />,
  } as NavLinkProps & { key: string };
}

/** The crosswalks whose names contain the filter, as list rows. */
function useCrosswalkLinks(
  options: Readonly<{
    crosswalks: readonly Crosswalk.T[];
    filter: string;
    workspaceSlug: string;
  }>,
): ReadonlyArray<NavLinkProps & { key: string }> {
  const { crosswalks, filter, workspaceSlug } = options;
  return useMemo(() => {
    const query = filter.trim().toLocaleLowerCase();
    return crosswalks
      .filter((crosswalk) => {
        return query === "" || crosswalk.name.toLocaleLowerCase().includes(query);
      })
      .map((crosswalk) => {
        return makeCrosswalkLink({ workspaceSlug, crosswalk });
      });
  }, [crosswalks, filter, workspaceSlug]);
}
```

### Task 15: The draft, its reducer, and loading a crosswalk

The crosswalk view edits one `CrosswalkDraft.T` and saves it whole. This task builds the three things under it: the `CrosswalkDraft` module (building a draft from the five tables, turning it into the save payload, counting datasets, and comparing two drafts), the reducer that applies every user action to the draft, and the two hooks that load what the view needs (`useCrosswalkContents` for the crosswalk's own rows, `useCrosswalkCatalog` for every dataset, column, dictionary entry, and binding it matches against).

The reducer is pure apart from minting ids (`uuid`) for layouts, columns, and mappings it creates. Task 16's `useCrosswalkFlow` therefore runs it once per dispatch, outside React's `useReducer` (which may call a reducer twice), and keeps the result in a ref, so the state a save sends is exactly the state on screen. Matching itself is all in Task 9's `CrosswalkMatch`: the reducer only decides which columns are open, which profiles to pass, and what status a layout ends with. Where the contract's reducer rules leave a case open, this task decides it as listed in the contract notes at the top of this part (the `saved` merge, carry-over sources, entry changes, statuses); each is pinned by a test below.

`useCrosswalkContents` waits for every query to have fetched since mount (or, offline, to be paused on its cached data) before it says `ready`. The persisted query cache can hold a crosswalk from before its last save, and a whole-set save built on that snapshot would undo the save, the reason `DataDictionaryView` refetches on mount. It reads the crosswalk with `useGetAll(where("id", "eq", ...))` rather than `useGetById`, so a missing crosswalk is an empty list (status `missing`) rather than an `undefined` query result, which TanStack Query treats as an error.

```ts
const COUNTY_COLUMN_ID = "22222222-0000-4000-8000-000000000002" as CrosswalkColumn.Id;
const MAPPING_ID = "33333333-0000-4000-8000-000000000001" as CrosswalkMapping.Id;

const DATASETS_BY_ID = new Map([
  [BRONX_ID, { name: "Bronx line list" }],
  [KINGS_APRIL_ID, { name: "Kings line list 2026-04" }],
  [KINGS_MARCH_ID, { name: "Kings line list 2026-03" }],
]);

function _layout(
  id: CrosswalkLayout.Id,
  columnNames: string[],
  overrides: Partial<CrosswalkLayout.T> = {},
): CrosswalkLayout.T {
  return {
    id,
    crosswalkId: CROSSWALK_ID,
    signature: CrosswalkLayout.buildSignature(columnNames),
    columnNames,
    isReference: false,
    status: "to_do",
    ...overrides,
  } as CrosswalkLayout.T;
}

const CONTENTS: CrosswalkDraft.Contents = {
  crosswalk: {
    id: CROSSWALK_ID,
    name: "Measles line lists",
    description: undefined,
    outputDatasetId: undefined,
    codesOutputAs: "labels",
    addsSourceColumn: true,
  } as Crosswalk.T,
  columns: [
    { id: COUNTY_COLUMN_ID, name: "county", position: 4, dataType: "varchar", entryId: undefined },
    { id: CASE_COLUMN_ID, name: "case_id", position: 1, dataType: "varchar", entryId: undefined },
  ] as CrosswalkColumn.T[],
  // Out of order on purpose: the draft sorts layouts and their datasets.
  layouts: [
    _layout(EMPTY_LAYOUT_ID, ["zip"]),
    _layout(KINGS_LAYOUT_ID, ["CaseNo", "county"], { status: "review" }),
    _layout(REFERENCE_ID, ["case_id", "county"], { isReference: true, status: "mapped" }),
  ],
  datasets: [
    { datasetId: KINGS_APRIL_ID, layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID },
    { datasetId: BRONX_ID, layoutId: REFERENCE_ID },
    { datasetId: KINGS_MARCH_ID, layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID },
  ] as CrosswalkDataset.T[],
  mappings: [
    {
      id: MAPPING_ID,
      layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID,
      columnId: CASE_COLUMN_ID,
      fill: {
        kind: "column",
        sourceColumn: "CaseNo",
        convert: undefined,
        codeListId: undefined,
        holdsLabels: false,
      },
      status: "suggested",
      confidence: 0.8,
      reason: "name_and_type",
    },
  ] as CrosswalkMapping.T[],
};

describe("CrosswalkDraft.makeEmpty", () => {
  it("starts unsaved, with labels, a source column, and nothing mapped", () => {
    expect(
      CrosswalkDraft.makeEmpty({ crosswalkId: CROSSWALK_ID, name: "Untitled crosswalk" }),
    ).toEqual({
      crosswalkId: CROSSWALK_ID,
      isSaved: false,
      name: "Untitled crosswalk",
      description: undefined,
      codesOutputAs: "labels",
      addsSourceColumn: true,
      outputDatasetId: undefined,
      columns: [],
      layouts: [],
      mappings: {},
    });
  });
});

describe("CrosswalkDraft.fromContents", () => {
  const draft = CrosswalkDraft.fromContents(CONTENTS, { datasetsById: DATASETS_BY_ID });

  it("orders columns by position and numbers them from 0", () => {
    expect(
      draft.columns.map((column) => {
        return [column.name, column.position];
      }),
    ).toEqual([
      ["case_id", 0],
      ["county", 1],
    ]);
  });

  it("puts the reference first, then layouts by first dataset name, empty last", () => {
    expect(
      draft.layouts.map((layout) => {
        return layout.id;
      }),
    ).toEqual([REFERENCE_ID, KINGS_LAYOUT_ID, EMPTY_LAYOUT_ID]);
  });

  it("sorts each layout's datasets by name and keys it by its column names", () => {
    const kings = draft.layouts[1];
    expect(kings?.datasetIds).toEqual([KINGS_MARCH_ID, KINGS_APRIL_ID]);
    expect(kings?.key).toBe(CrosswalkLayout.buildLayoutKey(["CaseNo", "county"]));
  });

  it("groups mappings by layout, then column", () => {
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.getFill(draft, KINGS_LAYOUT_ID, CASE_COLUMN_ID)).toEqual({
      id: MAPPING_ID,
      fill: CONTENTS.mappings[0]?.fill,
      status: "suggested",
      confidence: 0.8,
      reason: "name_and_type",
    });
    expect(draft.isSaved).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("CrosswalkDraft.toSavePayload", () => {
  const draft = CrosswalkDraft.fromContents(CONTENTS, { datasetsById: DATASETS_BY_ID });

  it("lists memberships by layout and mappings by layout then column", () => {
    const payload = CrosswalkDraft.toSavePayload({ ...draft, name: "  Measles  " });

    expect(payload.settings).toEqual({
      name: "Measles",
      description: undefined,
      codesOutputAs: "labels",
      addsSourceColumn: true,
    });
    expect(payload.datasets).toEqual([
      { datasetId: BRONX_ID, layoutId: REFERENCE_ID },
      { datasetId: KINGS_MARCH_ID, layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID },
      { datasetId: KINGS_APRIL_ID, layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID },
    ]);
    expect(payload.layouts[0]).toEqual({
      id: REFERENCE_ID,
      signature: CrosswalkLayout.buildSignature(["case_id", "county"]),
      columnNames: ["case_id", "county"],
      isReference: true,
      status: "mapped",
    });
    expect(payload.mappings).toEqual([
      {
        id: MAPPING_ID,
        layoutId: KINGS_LAYOUT_ID,
        columnId: CASE_COLUMN_ID,
        fill: CONTENTS.mappings[0]?.fill,
        status: "suggested",
        confidence: 0.8,
        reason: "name_and_type",
      },
    ]);
  });
});

describe("CrosswalkDraft helpers", () => {
  const draft = CrosswalkDraft.fromContents(CONTENTS, { datasetsById: DATASETS_BY_ID });

  it("counts the reference and mapped layouts as mapped", () => {
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.countDatasets(draft)).toEqual({
      total: 3,
      mapped: 1,
      skipped: 0,
      unconfirmed: 2,
    });
    const skippedKings = {
      ...draft,
      layouts: draft.layouts.map((layout) => {
        return layout.id === KINGS_LAYOUT_ID
          ? { ...layout, status: "skipped" as const }
          : layout;
      }),
    };
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.countDatasets(skippedKings)).toMatchObject({
      skipped: 2,
      unconfirmed: 0,
    });
  });

  it("finds the reference layout and every dataset", () => {
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.getReferenceLayout(draft)?.id).toBe(REFERENCE_ID);
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.getDatasetIds(draft)).toEqual([
      BRONX_ID,
      KINGS_MARCH_ID,
      KINGS_APRIL_ID,
    ]);
  });

  it("compares content, not whether it was saved or how a fill was built", () => {
    const rebuiltFill = {
      holdsLabels: false,
      codeListId: undefined,
      convert: undefined,
      sourceColumn: "CaseNo",
      kind: "column" as const,
    };
    const rebuilt: CrosswalkDraft.T = {
      ...draft,
      isSaved: false,
      mappings: {
        [KINGS_LAYOUT_ID]: {
          [CASE_COLUMN_ID]: {
            id: MAPPING_ID,
            fill: rebuiltFill,
            status: "suggested",
            confidence: 0.8,
            reason: "name_and_type",
          },
        },
      },
    };
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.isSameContent(draft, rebuilt)).toBe(true);
    expect(CrosswalkDraft.isSameContent(draft, { ...draft, name: "Other" })).toBe(false);
  });
});
```
