```tsx
import { useLingui } from "@lingui/react/macro";
import { useVirtualizer } from "@tanstack/react-virtual";
import { useId, useRef } from "react";
import css from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/MapLayoutsStep/LayoutStub/LayoutStub.module.css";
import { LayoutStubRow } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/MapLayoutsStep/LayoutStub/LayoutStubRow";
import { useLayoutListKeyboard } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/MapLayoutsStep/LayoutStub/useLayoutListKeyboard";
import type { CrosswalkLayout } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkLayout/CrosswalkLayout";
import type { CrosswalkDraft } from "@/lib/crosswalks/CrosswalkDraft/CrosswalkDraft";
import type { LayoutListKeyboard } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/MapLayoutsStep/LayoutStub/useLayoutListKeyboard";
import type { Virtualizer } from "@tanstack/react-virtual";
import type { ReactNode, RefObject } from "react";

/** Past this many layouts the stub renders only the rows in view. */
export const LAYOUT_STUB_VIRTUAL_THRESHOLD = 100;

/** A first guess at a row's height, corrected once each row is measured. */
const ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT_PX = 52;

type LayoutVirtualizer = Virtualizer<HTMLDivElement, Element>;

/** The stub's layouts, the selected one, and what selecting does. */
export type LayoutStubListProps = {
  layouts: readonly CrosswalkDraft.Layout[];
  datasetsById: ReadonlyMap<string, CrosswalkLayout.Dataset>;
  selectedLayoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id | undefined;
  /** Called on click, Enter, or Space; the caller saves a dirty draft first. */
  onSelectLayout: (layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id) => void;
};

type RowOptions = {
  props: Readonly<LayoutStubListProps>;
  keyboard: LayoutListKeyboard;
  getOptionId: (layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id) => string;
};

/** The virtualizer for a long list, or undefined for a short one. */
function _useLayoutVirtualizer(
  layouts: readonly CrosswalkDraft.Layout[],
  scrollerRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>,
): LayoutVirtualizer | undefined {
  const isVirtual = layouts.length > LAYOUT_STUB_VIRTUAL_THRESHOLD;
  const virtualizer = useVirtualizer({
    count: layouts.length,
    enabled: isVirtual,
    getScrollElement: () => {
      return scrollerRef.current;
    },
    estimateSize: () => {
      return ESTIMATED_ROW_HEIGHT_PX;
    },
    getItemKey: (index) => {
      return layouts[index]?.id ?? index;
    },
    overscan: 8,
  });
  return isVirtual ? virtualizer : undefined;
}

/** Scrolls a layout's row in through the virtualizer, for a long list only. */
function _makeScrollToLayout(
  virtualizer: LayoutVirtualizer | undefined,
  layoutIds: readonly CrosswalkLayout.Id[],
): ((layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id) => void) | undefined {
  if (!virtualizer) {
    return undefined;
  }
  return (layoutId) => {
    const index = layoutIds.indexOf(layoutId);
    if (index >= 0) {
      virtualizer.scrollToIndex(index, { align: "auto" });
    }
  };
}

/** One row, as the stub has always rendered it. */
function _renderRow(
  options: RowOptions & {
    layout: CrosswalkDraft.Layout;
    positionInList?: { position: number; count: number };
  },
): ReactNode {
  const { props, keyboard, layout } = options;
  return (
    <LayoutStubRow
      key={layout.id}
      layout={layout}
      datasetsById={props.datasetsById}
      optionId={options.getOptionId(layout.id)}
      isSelected={layout.id === props.selectedLayoutId}
      isActive={layout.id === keyboard.activeLayoutId}
      positionInList={options.positionInList}
      onSelect={() => {
        keyboard.setActiveLayoutId(layout.id);
        props.onSelectLayout(layout.id);
      }}
    />
  );
}

/** The rows in view, each in a wrapper the virtualizer measures and places. */
function _renderVirtualRows(
  options: RowOptions & { virtualizer: LayoutVirtualizer },
): ReactNode {
  const { props, virtualizer } = options;
  return (
    <div
      role="presentation"
      className={css.layoutStubListSizer}
      style={{ height: virtualizer.getTotalSize() }}
    >
      {virtualizer.getVirtualItems().map((item) => {
        const layout = props.layouts[item.index];
        return layout ? (
          <div
            key={layout.id}
            ref={virtualizer.measureElement}
            role="presentation"
            data-index={item.index}
            className={css.layoutStubVirtualRow}
            // Computed: each rendered row sits at its own measured offset.
            style={{ transform: `translateY(${item.start}px)` }}
          >
            {_renderRow({
              ...options,
              layout,
              positionInList: { position: item.index + 1, count: props.layouts.length },
            })}
          </div>
        ) : null;
      })}
    </div>
  );
}

/**
 * The stub's layouts as a single-select listbox that keeps focus itself and
 * points at its active row with `aria-activedescendant`, since a row out of
 * view is not in the DOM to hold focus. Past `LAYOUT_STUB_VIRTUAL_THRESHOLD`
 * layouts only the rows in view are rendered, each saying where it sits in
 * the whole list, and the active row is scrolled in through the
 * virtualizer. Named after the step.
 */
export function LayoutStubList(props: Readonly<LayoutStubListProps>): ReactNode {
  const { t } = useLingui();
  const listId = useId();
  const scrollerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const { layouts } = props;
  const virtualizer = _useLayoutVirtualizer(layouts, scrollerRef);
  const layoutIds = layouts.map((layout) => {
    return layout.id;
  });
  const getOptionId = (layoutId: CrosswalkLayout.Id): string => {
    return `${listId}-${layoutId}`;
  };
  const keyboard = useLayoutListKeyboard({
    layoutIds,
    selectedLayoutId: props.selectedLayoutId,
    getOptionId,
    onSelectLayout: props.onSelectLayout,
    scrollToLayout: _makeScrollToLayout(virtualizer, layoutIds),
  });
  const rowOptions: RowOptions = { props, keyboard, getOptionId };
  const { activeLayoutId } = keyboard;
  return (
    <div
      ref={scrollerRef}
      role="listbox"
      tabIndex={0}
      aria-label={t`Map each dataset`}
      aria-activedescendant={activeLayoutId ? getOptionId(activeLayoutId) : undefined}
      className={css.layoutStubList}
      onKeyDown={keyboard.onKeyDown}
    >
      {virtualizer
        ? _renderVirtualRows({ ...rowOptions, virtualizer })
        : layouts.map((layout) => {
            return _renderRow({ ...rowOptions, layout });
          })}
    </div>
  );
}
```

  `LayoutStubList` is 41 lines once formatted. The listbox keeps Task 19's label ("Map each dataset", the existing step label, so no new message), its class, and its id scheme. A short list never reads the virtualizer, which is created with `enabled: false` and so observes nothing; that is why Task 19's `LayoutStub.test.tsx` runs against the real `@tanstack/react-virtual` unchanged. The wrappers carry `role="presentation"`, so the accessibility tree still shows options directly under the listbox.

### Task 31: Combining progress per dataset

The first combine of a crosswalk reads every dataset it stacks, and relation loading acquires a query's uncached dependencies one at a time on purpose (`RelationLoading._fetchRelationBytes`: a virtual source's nested query loads tables the next source may read). With 100 datasets that is minutes of a spinner. Spec 9 promises "Step 3 shows progress per dataset". This task threads an optional `onRelationFetched?: (datasetId: Dataset.Id) => void` from `WorkspaceQuerySession.runQuery` down to relation loading and has the combined preview show "Read {count} of {total} datasets" with a `Progress` bar.

The call chain, read in the code as it is:

1. `WorkspaceQuerySession.runQuery` (`src/clients/qetl/WorkspaceQuerySession/WorkspaceQuerySession.ts`) passes its params to the mediator's `runQuery`.
2. `IQueryMediator.runQuery` (`src/clients/qetl/QueryMediator/QueryMediator.ts`) is `createQetlQueryRunner(state)`, whose `_runQuery` (`queryRunner.ts`) builds `RunLeasedQueryOptions` inside the lease and calls `_runLeasedQuery`, then `_loadQueryRelations`.
3. `_loadQueryRelations` asks `probeRelationCache` (`getRelationSources.ts`) which dependencies DuckDB cannot serve, then `_acquireRelations` asks `RelationLoading.probeStorageRelationCache` which of the rest the storage tier serves, and `RelationLoading.fetchRelationBytes` (`relationLoading/RelationLoading.ts`) acquires the remainder one by one through `_fetchRelationSource`.
4. A virtual source is acquired by `createRegistryForFetch`'s `runParquetQuery` (`relationLoading/createRegistryForFetch.ts`), which calls the same `runQuery` for its defining SQL under the outer lease, so its own dependencies go through steps 2 and 3 again.

The callback fires once per dataset as soon as its relation is in hand, wherever it came from: at once for a dataset DuckDB already serves (step 3's first probe), after the storage tier's bytes are read, and after a source returns its bytes. Reporting all three is what lets the count reach its total on a warm cache, where most datasets never reach a wrapper. A virtual dependency's nested query receives the same callback, so its sources report too; the preview counts only the datasets it stacks, so a nested report never pushes the count past the total. Nothing changes for a caller that passes no callback, and no public-session path passes one.

/**
 * Tells the caller each of these datasets is in hand, leaving out
 * `exceptIds`. A query without a callback reports nothing.

function _reportRelationsInHand(
  options: Readonly<{
    datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[];
    exceptIds?: readonly Dataset.Id[];
    onRelationFetched: RelationFetchedListener | undefined;
  }>,
): void {

```markdown
**Progress.** A caller may pass `onRelationFetched` to `runQuery`. It is
called once for each dataset the query loads, as soon as its relation is in
hand: after step 8 for one the queryable tier serves, after step 9 for a
storage tier hit, and after each source's bytes arrive in step 11. A
virtual dataset's nested query receives the same callback, so its sources
report too, and a caller that counts progress counts only the datasets it
asked about. A crosswalk's combined preview uses it to say how many of its
datasets are read.
```

- [ ] **Step 15: Write the hook and the bar.** `src/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/CombineStep/useCombiningProgress/useCombiningProgress.ts`:

```ts
import { useState } from "react";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

/** How many of the datasets a combine stacks are read so far. */
export type CombiningProgressCount = {
  readCount: number;
  totalCount: number;
};

/**
 * Counts the stacked datasets relation loading has in hand, from the
 * `onRelationFetched` reports of the combined preview's queries. A dataset
 * reported twice (by both preview queries, or by a nested virtual query)
 * counts once, and one the combine does not stack is not counted.
 */
export function useCombiningProgress(
  datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[],
): CombiningProgressCount & {
  onRelationFetched: (datasetId: Dataset.Id) => void;
  reset: () => void;
} {
  const [readIds, setReadIds] = useState<ReadonlySet<string>>(() => {
    return new Set();
  });
  return {
    readCount: datasetIds.filter((datasetId) => {
      return readIds.has(datasetId);
    }).length,
    totalCount: datasetIds.length,
    onRelationFetched: (datasetId) => {
      setReadIds((priorIds) => {
        return priorIds.has(datasetId)
          ? priorIds
          : new Set([...priorIds, datasetId]);
      });
    },
    reset: () => {
      setReadIds(new Set());
    },
  };
}
```

  `src/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/CombineStep/CombiningProgress/CombiningProgress.tsx`:

```tsx
import { plural } from "@lingui/core/macro";
import { useLingui } from "@lingui/react/macro";
import { Progress, Stack, Text } from "@mantine/core";
import type { CombiningProgressCount } from "@/views/DataManagerApp/CrosswalkView/CombineStep/useCombiningProgress/useCombiningProgress";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

/**
 * "Read 37 of 100 datasets" and a bar, while the combined preview reads
 * the datasets it stacks. The bar carries the same words as its name. It
 * sits inside the preview's reading status, which announces the count as
 * it changes, so it adds no live region of its own.
 */
export function CombiningProgress({
  readCount,
  totalCount,
}: Readonly<CombiningProgressCount>): ReactNode {
  const { i18n } = useLingui();
  const readLabel = i18n.number(readCount);
  const label = plural(totalCount, {
    one: `Read ${readLabel} of # dataset`,
    other: `Read ${readLabel} of # datasets`,
  });
  const percent =
    totalCount === 0 ? 0 : Math.round((readCount / totalCount) * 100);
  return (
    <Stack gap={4} w="100%" maw={360}>
      <Text size="sm" ta="center">
        {label}
      </Text>
      <Progress value={percent} aria-label={label} size="sm" />
    </Stack>
  );
}
```

  `aria-valuenow` is the percent; the test's 37 of 100 is 37 percent, which is why it reads `"37"`. The `w`/`maw` pair gives the bar a width inside the preview's centered reading state, whose `Stack` aligns its children to the center and would otherwise shrink the bar to nothing.

```ts
/**
 * Runs the preview's two queries, the first rows and then the row count,
 * reporting each dataset as relation loading has it in hand.
 */
async function _readCombinedPreview(
  options: Readonly<{
    workspaceId: Workspace.Id;
    sql: string;
    columnNames: readonly string[];
    onRelationFetched: (datasetId: Dataset.Id) => void;
  }>,
): Promise<CombinedPreviewResult> {
  const { workspaceId, columnNames, onRelationFetched } = options;
  const { rowsSql, countSql } = buildCombinedPreviewSql(options);
  const rows = await WorkspaceQuerySession.runQuery<Record<string, unknown>>({
    workspaceId,
    rawSql: rowsSql,
    onRelationFetched,
  });
  const count = await WorkspaceQuerySession.runQuery<{ rows: unknown }>({
    workspaceId,
    rawSql: countSql,
    onRelationFetched,
  });
  return {
    rows: rows.data.map((row) => {
      return _toPreviewRow(row, columnNames);
    }),
    rowCount: Number(count.data[0]?.rows ?? 0),
  };
}

/**
 * Reads the combined dataset's preview on this device: the first rows,
 * then the row count. The first read loads every source dataset, so it can
 * take minutes; `progress` counts the stacked datasets in hand meanwhile,
 * from none for each new read. Keyed by the SQL and its columns, so a
 * settings change reads again and a late reply is dropped; nothing is read
 * without SQL.
 */
export function useCombinedPreview(
  options: Readonly<{
    sql: string | undefined;
    columnNames: readonly string[];
    /** The datasets the SQL stacks, which the progress counts. */
    datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[];
  }>,
): CombinedPreviewRead {
  const workspace = useCurrentWorkspace();
  const { sql, columnNames } = options;
  const progress = useCombiningProgress(options.datasetIds);
  const read = useTaggedRead({
    key: sql === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify([sql, columnNames]),
    devMsg: "Reading the combined dataset preview failed",
    read: () => {
      progress.reset();
      return _readCombinedPreview({
        workspaceId: workspace.id,
        sql: sql ?? "",
        columnNames,
        onRelationFetched: progress.onRelationFetched,
      });
    },
  });
  return {
    ...read,
    progress: { readCount: progress.readCount, totalCount: progress.totalCount },
  };
}
```

  `buildCombinedPreviewSql` takes `{ sql, columnNames }` and ignores the other keys of the options it is passed. `useTaggedRead` runs `read` in an effect when the key changes, so `progress.reset()` runs there, never during render, and both `reset` and `onRelationFetched` only call `useCombiningProgress`'s state setter, so the closures `read` captured stay correct. A report from an older read still adds its dataset: that dataset is in hand on this device either way.

### Task 32: Measuring 100 datasets (open decision 4)

Spec 18 leaves one question to this slice: how long the first materialization of a combined dataset over 100 datasets takes, and whether that justifies parallel acquisition in relation loading. This task answers it with a measurement, not a guess. It adds a `performance.mark`/`measure` pair around each run of the combined preview (the first run after a page load is the cold materialization), logged in development, and two dev-only scripts: one seeds the branch's switched local stack with 100 small CSV-backed datasets in three layouts and one crosswalk mapped onto them, the other removes them. The steps run the preview cold, cold with a throttled network, warm from the storage tier, and hot from DuckDB, record the timings with the machine in `docs/measles-demo/crosswalks-materialization.md`, and apply a stated decision rule.

The seed writes data the way an upload does, so acquisition is the real path: each dataset is a `csv_file` dataset with `is_in_cloud_storage = true`, created through `rpc_datasets__add_csv_file_dataset` as the seeded workspace owner (the RPC uses `auth.uid()` and is granted to `authenticated` only), with its Parquet at `workspaces/<workspaceId>/datasets/<datasetId>.parquet`, uploaded with the service role, which is where `DatasetParquetStorageClient.downloadDataset` reads it. The Parquet is written by `@duckdb/node-api`, as `scripts/ai-eval/runtime/EvalDatabase.ts` already does under `pnpm vite-script`. The crosswalk row is inserted and saved through `rpc_crosswalks__save` as the same user, with fills built by the shared `CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson` and signatures by `CrosswalkLayout.buildSignature`, so the step-3 SQL is exactly what the app compiles.

Safety: both scripts refuse to run unless `SUPABASE_URL` (and `VITE_SUPABASE_API_URL`, when set) is a loopback address, and refuse while the worktree is switched to a hosted project (`AVA_SUPABASE_REMOTE_PROJECT_ID`), before reading any key or creating any client. They never run in CI and are not wired to any package script. The seed refuses to run twice (a crosswalk with its name exists) and points to the cleanup script.

The decision rule, set before measuring: **build parallel acquisition when the median cold first preview of 100 datasets, on the throttled network, exceeds 60 seconds and at least 70% of it is spent reading datasets** (the `readingMs` the measure records: from the start of the preview to the last dataset in hand). Over 60 seconds with reading under 70% means the time is in DuckDB stacking the rows, which parallel downloads would not shorten; that is recorded as its own follow-up instead. At or under 60 seconds, acquisition stays sequential and the progress bar from Task 31 is the answer.

```ts
import { Logger } from "@/utils/Logger";
import type { Dataset } from "$/models/datasets/Dataset/Dataset";

/**
 * The `performance` measure each run of a crosswalk's combined preview
 * records. Its `detail` holds `datasetCount`, `readCount`, and `readingMs`.
 * Read it in the browser with
 * `performance.getEntriesByName("crosswalks:combined-preview")`.
 */
export const COMBINED_PREVIEW_MEASURE = "crosswalks:combined-preview";

/** One run of the combined preview being timed. */
export type CombinedPreviewTiming = {
  /** Pass each `onRelationFetched` report of the run's queries. */
  onRelationFetched: (datasetId: Dataset.Id) => void;
  /** Records the measure once the run's queries are done, and logs it in development. */
  finish: (options: Readonly<{ datasetIds: readonly Dataset.Id[] }>) => void;
};

/**
 * Starts timing one run of the combined preview: the whole run, and the
 * part spent reading datasets (from the start to the last dataset in
 * hand). The measure lands in the browser's performance timeline in every
 * build; the log line appears in development only, since `Logger.log` is
 * silent in production.
 */
export function startCombinedPreviewTiming(): CombinedPreviewTiming {
  const runId = `${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 8)}`;
  const startMark = `${COMBINED_PREVIEW_MEASURE}:start:${runId}`;
  const startedAt = performance.now();
  const reading = { lastAt: startedAt, readIds: new Set<string>() };
  // jsdom's `performance` has only `now`, so a component test that runs
  // the preview must not fail on a missing User Timing API.
  const canMeasure =
    typeof performance.mark === "function" &&
    typeof performance.measure === "function";
  if (canMeasure) {
    performance.mark(startMark);
  }
  return {
    onRelationFetched: (datasetId) => {
      reading.lastAt = performance.now();
      reading.readIds.add(datasetId);
    },
    finish: ({ datasetIds }) => {
      const detail = {
        datasetCount: datasetIds.length,
        readCount: datasetIds.filter((datasetId) => {
          return reading.readIds.has(datasetId);
        }).length,
        readingMs: Math.round(reading.lastAt - startedAt),
      };
      if (canMeasure) {
        performance.measure(COMBINED_PREVIEW_MEASURE, { start: startMark, detail });
        performance.clearMarks(startMark);
      }
      Logger.log("[crosswalks] Combined preview", {
        totalMs: Math.round(performance.now() - startedAt),
        ...detail,
      });
    },
  };
}
```

/** Hostnames of this machine. `URL` keeps the brackets on an IPv6 host. */
const LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "127.0.0.1",
  "localhost",
  "[::1]",
]);

function _isLoopbackUrl(url: string): boolean {
  try {
    return LOOPBACK_HOSTNAMES.has(new URL(url).hostname);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * Why a measurement script must not run against this environment, or
 * undefined when it points only at a Supabase on this machine. Checked
 * before any key is read or any client is made, so a hosted project can
 * never be written to.
 */
export function getRemoteSupabaseRefusal(
  env: Readonly<Record<string, string | undefined>>,
): string | undefined {
  if (env.AVA_SUPABASE_REMOTE_PROJECT_ID) {
    return `This worktree is switched to the hosted Supabase project ${env.AVA_SUPABASE_REMOTE_PROJECT_ID}.`;
  }
  const serverUrl = env.SUPABASE_URL;
  if (!serverUrl) {
    return "SUPABASE_URL is not set.";
  }
  if (!_isLoopbackUrl(serverUrl)) {
    return `SUPABASE_URL (${serverUrl}) is not a Supabase on this machine.`;
  }
  const browserUrl = env.VITE_SUPABASE_API_URL;
  if (browserUrl !== undefined && !_isLoopbackUrl(browserUrl)) {
    return `VITE_SUPABASE_API_URL (${browserUrl}) is not a Supabase on this machine.`;
  }
  return undefined;
}

```ts
import { CrosswalkLayout } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkLayout/CrosswalkLayout";
import { CrosswalkMapping } from "$/models/crosswalks/CrosswalkMapping/CrosswalkMapping";
import type { AvaDataType } from "$/models/datasets/AvaDataType/AvaDataType";
import type { Json } from "$/types/database.types";

/** How many datasets the measurement seeds. */
export const MEASUREMENT_DATASET_COUNT = 100;

/** Rows in each seeded dataset: a large line list. */
export const MEASUREMENT_ROWS_PER_DATASET = 2_000;

/** Every seeded dataset's name starts with this, which is how cleanup finds them. */
export const MEASUREMENT_NAME_PREFIX = "Crosswalk measurement";

/** The seeded crosswalk's name, which is how the seed and cleanup find it. */
export const MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME = "Crosswalk measurement (100 datasets)";

type MeasurementColumn = {
  name: string;
  dataType: AvaDataType.T;
  duckDbType: "VARCHAR" | "BIGINT" | "DATE";
  /** The column's value for row `i` of `range(rowCount)`. */
  valueSql: string;
};

/** One layout the measurement seeds: its datasets share these columns. */
export type MeasurementLayout = {
  key: "kings" | "queens" | "bronx";
  datasetCount: number;
  columns: readonly MeasurementColumn[];
};

const ONSET_SQL = "DATE '2026-01-01' + CAST(i % 120 AS INTEGER)";

/** Three layouts, as a state's counties might send line lists: 50, 35, and 15 datasets. */
export const MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS: readonly MeasurementLayout[] = [
  {
    key: "kings",
    datasetCount: 50,
    columns: [
      { name: "case_id", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "'K-' || CAST(i AS VARCHAR)" },
      { name: "sex", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "CASE i % 2 WHEN 0 THEN 'Male' ELSE 'Female' END" },
      { name: "rash_onset_date", dataType: "date", duckDbType: "DATE", valueSql: ONSET_SQL },
      { name: "zip_code", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "CAST(10451 + i % 50 AS VARCHAR)" },
      { name: "county", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "'Kings'" },
    ],
  },
  {
    key: "queens",
    datasetCount: 35,
    columns: [
      { name: "CaseNo", dataType: "bigint", duckDbType: "BIGINT", valueSql: "i" },
      { name: "GENDER", dataType: "bigint", duckDbType: "BIGINT", valueSql: "1 + i % 2" },
      { name: "onset_dt", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: `strftime(${ONSET_SQL}, '%m/%d/%Y')` },
      { name: "zip", dataType: "bigint", duckDbType: "BIGINT", valueSql: "501 + i % 50" },
    ],
  },
  {
    key: "bronx",
    datasetCount: 15,
    columns: [
      { name: "id", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "'B-' || CAST(i AS VARCHAR)" },
      { name: "sex_cd", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "CASE i % 2 WHEN 0 THEN 'M' ELSE 'F' END" },
      { name: "rash_onset", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: `strftime(${ONSET_SQL}, '%Y-%m-%d')` },
      { name: "postal_code", dataType: "varchar", duckDbType: "VARCHAR", valueSql: "CAST(11201 + i % 30 AS VARCHAR)" },
      { name: "age_mo", dataType: "bigint", duckDbType: "BIGINT", valueSql: "6 + i % 200" },
    ],
  },
];

/** One dataset the measurement seeds. */
export type MeasurementDataset = {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  layoutKey: MeasurementLayout["key"];
};

/** Every seeded dataset, layout by layout, named `Crosswalk measurement <layout> <nn>`. */
export function buildMeasurementDatasets(
  makeId: () => string,
): MeasurementDataset[] {
  return MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS.flatMap((layout) => {
    return Array.from({ length: layout.datasetCount }, (_item, index) => {
      const number = String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0");
      return {
        id: makeId(),
        name: `${MEASUREMENT_NAME_PREFIX} ${layout.key} ${number}`,
        layoutKey: layout.key,
      };
    });
  });
}

/** A `COPY` that writes one layout's rows to a Parquet file. */
export function buildParquetSql(
  options: Readonly<{ layout: MeasurementLayout; rowCount: number; outputPath: string }>,
): string {
  const selects = options.layout.columns.map((column) => {
    return `CAST(${column.valueSql} AS ${column.duckDbType}) AS "${column.name}"`;
  });
  const path = options.outputPath.replaceAll("'", "''");
  return `COPY (SELECT ${selects.join(", ")} FROM range(${options.rowCount}) AS t(i)) TO '${path}' (FORMAT parquet)`;
}

/** One layout's columns as `rpc_datasets__add_csv_file_dataset` takes them. */
export function toDatasetColumnInputs(layout: MeasurementLayout) {
  return layout.columns.map((column, index) => {
    return {
      original_name: column.name,
      name: column.name,
      description: null,
      original_data_type: column.duckDbType,
      detected_data_type: column.duckDbType,
      data_type: column.dataType,
      column_idx: index,
    };
  });
}

/** The combined dataset's columns, from the reference (Kings) layout. */
const COMBINED_COLUMNS = MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS[0]!.columns.map((column) => {
  return { name: column.name, dataType: column.dataType };
});

function _columnFill(
  sourceColumn: string,
  convert?: CrosswalkMapping.Convert,
): CrosswalkMapping.Fill {
  return { kind: "column", sourceColumn, convert, codeListId: undefined, holdsLabels: false };
}

/** How each layout fills each combined column, in `COMBINED_COLUMNS` order. */
const FILLS_BY_LAYOUT: Record<MeasurementLayout["key"], readonly CrosswalkMapping.Fill[]> = {
  kings: COMBINED_COLUMNS.map((column) => {
    return _columnFill(column.name);
  }),
  queens: [
    _columnFill("CaseNo"),
    _columnFill("GENDER"),
    _columnFill("onset_dt", { kind: "parse_date", format: "%m/%d/%Y" }),
    _columnFill("zip", { kind: "pad_text", length: 5 }),
    { kind: "constant", value: "Queens" },
  ],
  bronx: [
    _columnFill("id"),
    _columnFill("sex_cd"),
    _columnFill("rash_onset", { kind: "parse_date", format: "%Y-%m-%d" }),
    _columnFill("postal_code"),
    { kind: "empty" },
  ],
};

/**
 * The parameters of `rpc_crosswalks__save` for the seeded crosswalk: the
 * Kings layout as the mapped reference, the Queens and Bronx layouts
 * mapped with conversions, a fixed value, and an empty column, and every
 * dataset in its layout.
 */
export function buildMeasurementSaveParams(
  options: Readonly<{ crosswalkId: string; datasets: readonly MeasurementDataset[]; makeId: () => string }>,
) {
  const columns = COMBINED_COLUMNS.map((column, position) => {
    return { id: options.makeId(), name: column.name, position, data_type: column.dataType, entry_id: null };
  });
  const layouts = MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS.map((layout, index) => {
    const columnNames = layout.columns.map((column) => {
      return column.name;
    });
    return {
      id: options.makeId(),
      key: layout.key,
      signature: CrosswalkLayout.buildSignature(columnNames),
      column_names: columnNames,
      is_reference: index === 0,
      status: "mapped" as const,
    };
  });
  return {
    p_crosswalk_id: options.crosswalkId,
    p_settings: { name: MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME, description: null, codes_output_as: "labels", adds_source_column: true },
    p_columns: columns,
    p_layouts: layouts.map(({ key: _key, ...layout }) => {
      return layout;
    }),
    p_datasets: options.datasets.map((dataset) => {
      const layout = layouts.find((candidate) => {
        return candidate.key === dataset.layoutKey;
      });
      return { dataset_id: dataset.id, layout_id: layout!.id };
    }),
    p_mappings: _buildMappings({ columns, layouts, makeId: options.makeId }),
  };
}

function _buildMappings(
  options: Readonly<{
    columns: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string }>;
    layouts: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; key: MeasurementLayout["key"] }>;
    makeId: () => string;
  }>,
) {
  return options.layouts.flatMap((layout) => {
    return options.columns.map((column, index) => {
      return {
        id: options.makeId(),
        layout_id: layout.id,
        column_id: column.id,
        fill: CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson(FILLS_BY_LAYOUT[layout.key][index]!) as Json,
        status: "confirmed" as const,
        confidence: null,
        reason: null,
      };
    });
  });
}
```

  `buildMeasurementSaveParams` and `toDatasetColumnInputs` leave their return types to inference on purpose: they are the RPCs' argument shapes, which the seed script passes to the typed Supabase client, so a mismatch with `database.types.ts` shows up as a type error there. `fillToDBJson` returns Task 7's `StoredCrosswalkFill`; the `as Json` keeps the mapping literal a plain `Json` value whatever zod infers for its optional parts. If oxfmt splits `buildMeasurementSaveParams` past 45 lines, move the `p_datasets` mapping into `_buildMemberships({ datasets, layouts })`.

- [ ] **Step 15: Write the output helpers.** `scripts/crosswalks/measurementOutput.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Terminal output for the crosswalk measurement scripts: progress,
 * results, and errors go to stderr, so stdout holds only a script's
 * documented result. Plain text when stderr is not a terminal, `NO_COLOR`
 * is set, or `TERM` is `dumb`.
 */
const IS_PLAIN =
  !process.stderr.isTTY ||
  Boolean(process.env.NO_COLOR) ||
  process.env.TERM === "dumb";

const THEME = { accent: "36", success: "32", warning: "33", error: "31", heading: "1" } as const;

function _paint(role: keyof typeof THEME, text: string): string {
  return IS_PLAIN ? text : `\u001b[${THEME[role]}m${text}\u001b[0m`;
}

function _write(line: string): void {
  process.stderr.write(`${line}\n`);
}

/** Prints the measurement scripts' progress, results, and errors. */
export const MeasurementOutput = {
  /** Announces work before it starts. */
  step: (message: string): void => {
    _write(`${_paint("accent", "→")} ${message}`);
  },
  success: (message: string): void => {
    _write(_paint("success", `✅ ${message}`));
  },
  warn: (message: string): void => {
    _write(_paint("warning", `⚠️ ${message}`));
  },
  /** Prints an error and how to recover, and marks the run as failed. */
  fail: (options: Readonly<{ script: string; message: string; hint: string }>): void => {
    _write(_paint("error", `❌ ${options.script}: ${options.message}`));
    _write(_paint("warning", `  ⚠️ ${options.hint}`));
    process.exitCode = 1;
  },
};

/**
 * Handles a script's arguments: `-h` or `--help` prints `help` to stdout;
 * anything else prints the usage and a hint to stderr and fails, since the
 * measurement scripts take no options. Returns true when the script should
 * run. A `--` from `pnpm vite-script` is ignored.
 */
export function shouldRunScript(
  options: Readonly<{ script: string; argv: readonly string[]; help: string }>,
): boolean {
  const args = options.argv.filter((arg) => {
    return arg !== "--";
  });
  if (args.includes("-h") || args.includes("--help")) {
    process.stdout.write(`${options.help}\n`);
    return false;
  }
  if (args.length > 0) {
    process.stderr.write(`${options.help}\n\n`);
    MeasurementOutput.fail({
      script: options.script,
      message: `Unknown arguments: ${args.join(" ")}`,
      hint: "This script takes no options. Run it with none, or with --help.",
    });
    return false;
  }
  return true;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 16: Write the seed script.** `scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Seeds this branch's local Supabase with 100 CSV-backed datasets in three
 * layouts and a crosswalk mapped onto them, to measure the combined
 * preview at scale. Local only: it refuses any Supabase not on this
 * machine. Run with:
 *
 *   dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts
 */
import { mkdtempSync, readFileSync, rmSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { promiseMapSequential } from "@avandar/utils";
import { DuckDBInstance } from "@duckdb/node-api";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { TEST_USER_EMAIL, TEST_USER_PASSWORD, TEST_WORKSPACE_SLUG } from "seed/SeedData";
import {
  buildMeasurementDatasets,
  buildMeasurementSaveParams,
  buildParquetSql,
  MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME,
  MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS,
  MEASUREMENT_ROWS_PER_DATASET,
  toDatasetColumnInputs,
} from "./crosswalkMeasurementPlan/crosswalkMeasurementPlan";
import { MeasurementOutput, shouldRunScript } from "./measurementOutput";
import { getRemoteSupabaseRefusal } from "./requireLocalSupabase/requireLocalSupabase";
import type { MeasurementDataset, MeasurementLayout } from "./crosswalkMeasurementPlan/crosswalkMeasurementPlan";
import type { AvaSupabaseDBClient } from "$/types/AvaSupabaseDbClient.types";
import type { Database } from "$/types/database.types";

const SCRIPT = "seedCrosswalkMeasurement";
const HELP = `Seeds this branch's local Supabase with 100 CSV-backed datasets in three
layouts (50, 35, 15) and a crosswalk mapped onto them, to measure the
combined preview. Refuses any Supabase that is not on this machine.

Usage:
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts [-h|--help]

Options:
  -h, --help   Show this help and exit.

Output:
  stdout: the crosswalk's step-3 URL. Progress goes to stderr.

Examples:
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts > .temp/feat-crosswalks/crosswalk-url.txt

Remove what it seeds with scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts.`;

const PARQUET_TYPE = "application/vnd.apache.parquet";

type SeedClients = { admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient; user: AvaSupabaseDBClient; userId: string };

function _readEnv(name: string): string {
  const value = process.env[name];
  if (!value) {
    throw new Error(`${name} is not set. Run the script through dotenv -e .env.development.`);
  }
  return value;
}

async function _createClients(): Promise<SeedClients> {
  const url = _readEnv("SUPABASE_URL");
  const options = { auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false } };
  const admin = createClient<Database>(url, _readEnv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"), options);
  const user = createClient<Database>(url, _readEnv("VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY"), options);
  const { data, error } = await user.auth.signInWithPassword({
    email: TEST_USER_EMAIL,
    password: TEST_USER_PASSWORD,
  });
  if (error || !data.user) {
    throw new Error(`Could not sign in as ${TEST_USER_EMAIL}: ${error?.message ?? "no user"}`);
  }
  return { admin, user, userId: data.user.id };
}

async function _getWorkspace(
  clients: SeedClients,
): Promise<{ workspaceId: string; profileId: string }> {
  const { data: workspace } = await clients.user
    .from("workspaces")
    .select("id")
    .eq("slug", TEST_WORKSPACE_SLUG)
    .single()
    .throwOnError();
  const { data: profile } = await clients.user
    .from("user_profiles")
    .select("id")
    .eq("user_id", clients.userId)
    .eq("workspace_id", workspace.id)
    .single()
    .throwOnError();
  return { workspaceId: workspace.id, profileId: profile.id };
}

async function _isAlreadySeeded(admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient): Promise<boolean> {
  const { data } = await admin
    .from("crosswalks")
    .select("id")
    .eq("name", MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME)
    .throwOnError();
  return data.length > 0;
}

/** One Parquet file per layout, written by node DuckDB into a temporary folder. */
async function _writeParquetFiles(
  folder: string,
): Promise<Map<MeasurementLayout["key"], Uint8Array>> {
  const instance = await DuckDBInstance.create(":memory:");
  const connection = await instance.connect();
  try {
    const entries = await promiseMapSequential(MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS, async (layout) => {
      const outputPath = join(folder, `${layout.key}.parquet`);
      await connection.run(
        buildParquetSql({ layout, rowCount: MEASUREMENT_ROWS_PER_DATASET, outputPath }),
      );
      return [layout.key, new Uint8Array(readFileSync(outputPath))] as const;
    });
    return new Map(entries);
  } finally {
    connection.closeSync();
  }
}

async function _createDataset(
  options: Readonly<{
    clients: SeedClients;
    workspaceId: string;
    dataset: MeasurementDataset;
    bytes: Uint8Array;
  }>,
): Promise<void> {
  const { clients, workspaceId, dataset, bytes } = options;
  const layout = MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS.find((candidate) => {
    return candidate.key === dataset.layoutKey;
  })!;
  await clients.user
    .rpc("rpc_datasets__add_csv_file_dataset", {
      p_dataset_id: dataset.id,
      p_workspace_id: workspaceId,
      p_dataset_name: dataset.name,
      p_dataset_description: "Seeded to measure a crosswalk's combined preview.",
      p_columns: toDatasetColumnInputs(layout),
      p_is_in_cloud_storage: true,
      p_size_in_bytes: bytes.byteLength,
      p_rows_to_skip: 0,
      p_quote_char: { value: '"' },
      p_escape_char: { value: '"' },
      p_delimiter: ",",
      p_newline_delimiter: "\n",
      p_comment_char: { value: null },
      p_has_header: true,
      p_date_format: { date_format: null, timestamp_format: null },
    })
    .throwOnError();
  const { error } = await clients.admin.storage
    .from("workspaces")
    .upload(`${workspaceId}/datasets/${dataset.id}.parquet`, new Blob([bytes], { type: PARQUET_TYPE }), {
      contentType: PARQUET_TYPE,
      upsert: true,
    });
  if (error) {
    throw new Error(`Could not upload ${dataset.name}'s Parquet: ${error.message}`);
  }
}

async function _createDatasets(
  options: Readonly<{
    clients: SeedClients;
    workspaceId: string;
    datasets: readonly MeasurementDataset[];
    bytesByLayout: ReadonlyMap<MeasurementLayout["key"], Uint8Array>;
  }>,
): Promise<void> {
  // One at a time, so a failure stops at the dataset that failed and the
  // progress lines stay in order.
  await promiseMapSequential([...options.datasets.entries()], async ([index, dataset]) => {
    await _createDataset({ ...options, dataset, bytes: options.bytesByLayout.get(dataset.layoutKey)! });
    if ((index + 1) % 10 === 0) {
      MeasurementOutput.step(`Seeded ${index + 1} of ${options.datasets.length} datasets`);
    }
  });
}

async function _createCrosswalk(
  options: Readonly<{
    clients: SeedClients;
    workspaceId: string;
    profileId: string;
    datasets: readonly MeasurementDataset[];
  }>,
): Promise<string> {
  const { clients } = options;
  const { data: crosswalk } = await clients.user
    .from("crosswalks")
    .insert({
      workspace_id: options.workspaceId,
      owner_id: clients.userId,
      owner_profile_id: options.profileId,
      name: MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME,
    })
    .select("id")
    .single()
    .throwOnError();
  await clients.user
    .rpc(
      "rpc_crosswalks__save",
      buildMeasurementSaveParams({ crosswalkId: crosswalk.id, datasets: options.datasets, makeId: () => {
        return crypto.randomUUID();
      } }),
    )
    .throwOnError();
  return crosswalk.id;
}

async function _seed(): Promise<string> {
  MeasurementOutput.step("Signing in as the seeded workspace owner");
  const clients = await _createClients();
  if (await _isAlreadySeeded(clients.admin)) {
    throw new Error("ALREADY_SEEDED");
  }
  const { workspaceId, profileId } = await _getWorkspace(clients);
  const folder = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "crosswalk-measurement-"));
  try {
    MeasurementOutput.step(`Writing ${MEASUREMENT_LAYOUTS.length} Parquet files of ${MEASUREMENT_ROWS_PER_DATASET} rows`);
    const bytesByLayout = await _writeParquetFiles(folder);
    const datasets = buildMeasurementDatasets(() => {
      return crypto.randomUUID();
    });
    MeasurementOutput.step(`Creating ${datasets.length} datasets and uploading their Parquet`);
    await _createDatasets({ clients, workspaceId, datasets, bytesByLayout });
    MeasurementOutput.step("Creating and saving the crosswalk");
    return await _createCrosswalk({ clients, workspaceId, profileId, datasets });
  } finally {
    rmSync(folder, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  if (!shouldRunScript({ script: SCRIPT, argv: process.argv.slice(2), help: HELP })) {
    return;
  }
  const refusal = getRemoteSupabaseRefusal(process.env);
  if (refusal) {
    MeasurementOutput.fail({ script: SCRIPT, message: refusal, hint: "Run ava supabase status, switch this branch to its own local stack with ava supabase switch, and retry." });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const crosswalkId = await _seed();
    const appUrl = process.env.VITE_APP_URL ?? "";
    MeasurementOutput.success("Seeded 100 datasets and the crosswalk.");
    process.stdout.write(`${appUrl}/${TEST_WORKSPACE_SLUG}/data-manager/crosswalks/${crosswalkId}?step=combine\n`);
  } catch (error) {
    const isSeeded = error instanceof Error && error.message === "ALREADY_SEEDED";
    MeasurementOutput.fail({
      script: SCRIPT,
      message: isSeeded ? `${MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME} already exists.` : String(error instanceof Error ? error.message : error),
      hint: "Run dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts, then retry.",
    });
  }
}

void main();
```

  Notes for the implementer: `p_escape_char` and `p_quote_char` take the `util__nullable_text` composite, as `createDatasetMutations.ts` sends them; `{ value: null }` is "none". If `connection.closeSync` does not exist in `@duckdb/node-api` 1.5.5, use the close call `scripts/ai-eval/runtime/EvalDatabase.ts` uses. Task 5's generated `Database["public"]["Functions"]["rpc_crosswalks__save"]["Args"]` is `{ p_crosswalk_id: string; p_settings: Json; p_columns: Json; p_layouts: Json; p_datasets: Json; p_mappings: Json }`, and `buildMeasurementSaveParams` returns plain object and array literals of strings, numbers, booleans, and `null` (no `undefined`, no readonly arrays), which are assignable to `Json`, so the call needs no cast. Its snake_case keys are the ones Task 13's `_toSaveRpcArgs` sends (`name`, `description`, `codes_output_as`, `adds_source_column`; `id`, `name`, `position`, `data_type`, `entry_id`; `id`, `signature`, `column_names`, `is_reference`, `status`; `dataset_id`, `layout_id`; `id`, `layout_id`, `column_id`, `fill`, `status`, `confidence`, `reason`), with each fill through `CrosswalkMapping.fillToDBJson`, so the RPC sees exactly what the app saves. `crypto.randomUUID` is a Node global.

- [ ] **Step 17: Write the cleanup script.** `scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts`:

```ts
/**
 * Removes what seedCrosswalkMeasurement seeded from this branch's local
 * Supabase: the crosswalk, its combined dataset if one was created, every
 * dataset named "Crosswalk measurement ...", and their Parquet files. Local
 * only: it refuses any Supabase not on this machine. Run with:
 *
 *   dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts
 */
import { promiseMapSequential } from "@avandar/utils";
import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";
import { TEST_WORKSPACE_SLUG } from "seed/SeedData";
import { MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME, MEASUREMENT_NAME_PREFIX } from "./crosswalkMeasurementPlan/crosswalkMeasurementPlan";
import { MeasurementOutput, shouldRunScript } from "./measurementOutput";
import { getRemoteSupabaseRefusal } from "./requireLocalSupabase/requireLocalSupabase";
import type { AvaSupabaseDBClient } from "$/types/AvaSupabaseDbClient.types";
import type { Database } from "$/types/database.types";

const SCRIPT = "cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement";
const HELP = `Removes the crosswalk measurement's crosswalk, its combined dataset, the
100 "Crosswalk measurement ..." datasets, and their Parquet files from this
branch's local Supabase. Refuses any Supabase that is not on this machine.

Usage:
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts [-h|--help]

Options:
  -h, --help   Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts
  dotenv -e .env.development -- pnpm vite-script scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts --help`;

/** Storage removes at most this many objects per call here. */
const REMOVE_BATCH_SIZE = 100;

async function _findSeeded(admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient): Promise<{
  workspaceId: string;
  crosswalkIds: string[];
  datasetIds: string[];
}> {
  const { data: workspace } = await admin.from("workspaces").select("id").eq("slug", TEST_WORKSPACE_SLUG).single().throwOnError();
  const { data: crosswalks } = await admin
    .from("crosswalks")
    .select("id, output_dataset_id")
    .eq("workspace_id", workspace.id)
    .eq("name", MEASUREMENT_CROSSWALK_NAME)
    .throwOnError();
  const { data: datasets } = await admin
    .from("datasets")
    .select("id")
    .eq("workspace_id", workspace.id)
    .like("name", `${MEASUREMENT_NAME_PREFIX} %`)
    .throwOnError();
  const outputIds = crosswalks.flatMap((crosswalk) => {
    return crosswalk.output_dataset_id ? [crosswalk.output_dataset_id] : [];
  });
  return {
    workspaceId: workspace.id,
    crosswalkIds: crosswalks.map((crosswalk) => {
      return crosswalk.id;
    }),
    datasetIds: [...new Set([...outputIds, ...datasets.map((dataset) => {
      return dataset.id;
    })])],
  };
}

async function _removeParquet(
  admin: AvaSupabaseDBClient,
  workspaceId: string,
  datasetIds: readonly string[],
): Promise<void> {
  const batches = Array.from({ length: Math.ceil(datasetIds.length / REMOVE_BATCH_SIZE) }, (_item, index) => {
    return datasetIds.slice(index * REMOVE_BATCH_SIZE, (index + 1) * REMOVE_BATCH_SIZE);
  });
  await promiseMapSequential(batches, async (batch) => {
    const paths = batch.map((datasetId) => {
      return `${workspaceId}/datasets/${datasetId}.parquet`;
    });
    const { error } = await admin.storage.from("workspaces").remove(paths);
    if (error) {
      throw new Error(`Could not remove Parquet files: ${error.message}`);
    }
  });
}

async function _cleanUp(): Promise<{ crosswalkCount: number; datasetCount: number }> {
  const admin = createClient<Database>(process.env.SUPABASE_URL ?? "", process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ?? "", {
    auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false },
  });
  MeasurementOutput.step("Finding the seeded crosswalk and datasets");
  const seeded = await _findSeeded(admin);
  MeasurementOutput.step(`Deleting ${seeded.crosswalkIds.length} crosswalk and ${seeded.datasetIds.length} datasets`);
  if (seeded.crosswalkIds.length > 0) {
    await admin.from("crosswalks").delete().in("id", seeded.crosswalkIds).throwOnError();
  }
  if (seeded.datasetIds.length > 0) {
    await admin.from("datasets").delete().in("id", seeded.datasetIds).throwOnError();
    MeasurementOutput.step("Removing their Parquet files");
    await _removeParquet(admin, seeded.workspaceId, seeded.datasetIds);
  }
  return { crosswalkCount: seeded.crosswalkIds.length, datasetCount: seeded.datasetIds.length };
}

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  if (!shouldRunScript({ script: SCRIPT, argv: process.argv.slice(2), help: HELP })) {
    return;
  }
  const refusal = getRemoteSupabaseRefusal(process.env);
  if (refusal) {
    MeasurementOutput.fail({ script: SCRIPT, message: refusal, hint: "Run ava supabase status, point this worktree at its local stack, and retry." });
    return;
  }
  if (!process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) {
    MeasurementOutput.fail({ script: SCRIPT, message: "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is not set.", hint: "Run the script through dotenv -e .env.development." });
    return;
  }
  try {
    const removed = await _cleanUp();
    MeasurementOutput.success(`Removed ${removed.crosswalkCount} crosswalk and ${removed.datasetCount} datasets.`);
  } catch (error) {
    MeasurementOutput.fail({
      script: SCRIPT,
      message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
      hint: "Fix the cause above and run the cleanup again: it only removes what is still there.",
    });
  }
}

void main();
```

  A Parquet file whose object is already gone is not an error for `storage.remove`, so a second run after a partial failure finishes the job.

```markdown
# Crosswalk materialization at 100 datasets

Measured for open decision 4 of
[data-dictionaries-design.md](data-dictionaries-design.md): how long the
first combine of a crosswalk over 100 datasets takes, and whether relation
loading should acquire a query's datasets in parallel.

## Setup

- 100 CSV-backed datasets of 2,000 rows each (200,000 rows), in three
  layouts of 50, 35, and 15 datasets, and one crosswalk mapping all three
  onto five columns, with two date parses, ZIP padding, a fixed value, and
  an empty column. Seeded by `scripts/crosswalks/seedCrosswalkMeasurement.ts`
  into the branch's switched local Supabase; removed by
  `scripts/crosswalks/cleanupCrosswalkMeasurement.ts`.
- Each dataset's Parquet is downloaded from local Supabase Storage, so the
  unthrottled cold run has almost no network cost. The throttled run uses
  DevTools' Fast 4G profile (150 ms latency, 9 Mbps down) to stand in for a
  real connection.
- The timing is the `crosswalks:combined-preview` performance measure
  around the preview's two queries (`SELECT * ... LIMIT 20` and the row
  count). `readingMs` runs from the start of the preview to the last
  dataset in hand.
- Machine: <CPU>, <memory> GB, macOS <version>, Playwright Chromium
  <version>, headless. Branch commit `<git rev-parse --short HEAD>`.

## Results

| Run | Total (s) | Reading (s) | Reading share |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold, throttled | <s> | <s> | <percent> |
| Cold, unthrottled | <s> | <s> | <percent> |
| Warm, storage tier | <s> | <s> | <percent> |
| Hot, DuckDB | <s> | <s> | <percent> |

<One or two sentences on anything the runs showed beyond the numbers, such
as memory pressure or a crash, or "Nothing else of note.">

## Decision

The rule, set before measuring: build parallel acquisition when the median
cold, throttled first preview exceeds 60 seconds and at least 70% of it is
reading datasets. Over 60 seconds with reading under 70% means the time is
in DuckDB stacking the rows, which parallel downloads would not shorten.

<One of:
"Cold, throttled took <s> s, under 60 s: relation loading keeps acquiring
one dataset at a time. Step 3's per-dataset progress covers the wait."
"Cold, throttled took <s> s with <percent> reading: parallel acquisition is
worth building, as a follow-up feature on the roadmap."
"Cold, throttled took <s> s but only <percent> reading: parallel
acquisition would not help; the stacking query is the follow-up.">
```

## Executing this plan in batches

The tasks are ordered so each batch can go to one subagent, which runs its tasks one at a time ("any order" means the order within that one subagent), with independent batches in parallel. No two batches that run alongside each other change the same file. Task 0 runs first, by the coordinating session. Parallel batches share one worktree: each commits only its own paths, by name, and retries a commit that meets `index.lock`.

| Batch | Tasks | Needs | Runs alongside |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S: schema | 1, 2, 3, 4, then 5 | Task 0, with `ava supabase status` naming `feat-crosswalks` | none |
| M: models and pure logic | 6, 7, then 8, 9, 10 (in order), then 11, 12 | S (Task 5's generated types) | C, once Tasks 6 and 7 are committed |
| C: clients and navigation | 13, 14 | M's Tasks 6 and 7 | M's Tasks 8 to 12 |
| D: draft and shell | 15, then 16 | M, C | none |
| U1: step 1 and reading values | 17, 18 | D | U2 |
| U2: stub and table | 19, 20 | D | U1 |
| U3: pane, step 2, step 3 | 21, then 22, then 23 | U1, U2 | none |
| F: finish Part A | 24, 25 (any order), then 26, 27, 28 | U3 | none |
| B: Part B | 29, 30, 31 (any order), then 32, 33 | F, or the merged Part A | none |

Every batch ends with its own tests green and a commit per task. Review between batches with the `avandar-code-review` skill.

## Refinements made while planning

These override the spec where they differ.

- **Stale detection uses a fingerprint of the pairs, not `updated_at`.** `data_dictionaries__write_code_lists` upserts every list of a dictionary on every save, so a list's `updated_at` moves even when its pairs did not, and spec 5.4's `compiled_code_list_versions` would raise the banner after any dictionary edit. `crosswalks.compiled_code_lists` stores `[{ code_list_id, fingerprint }]`: an array, because the parsers' `camelCaseKeysDeep` would rewrite uuid object keys.
- **Signatures and fingerprints are FNV-1a 64 hashes,** computed synchronously in shared TypeScript (`fnv1a64Hex`), so the reducer and the stale check need no async hashing. They only group and compare; nothing relies on them being cryptographic.
- **The children are select-only and saved whole.** Spec 11 gave Data Sources editors insert and update on every crosswalk table. As with dictionaries, the four child tables are select-only for signed-in users and written only by `rpc_crosswalks__save`, so a crosswalk is never half-saved (a column deleted while its mappings remain, two reference layouts).
- **A whole save never removes what the caller cannot see.** `crosswalks__datasets` rows are readable only by someone who can view the dataset, and the save keeps any membership whose dataset the caller cannot view, so one editor's save never drops another's restricted dataset.
- **`crosswalks__datasets` has its own `id`,** with `unique (crosswalk_id, dataset_id)`, because `createRdbCrudClient` needs a single-column key.
- **A mapping's `reason` is an enum key, translated in the UI,** with a fourth value, `similar_layout`, for a fill carried over from a similar layout (spec 8.3).
- **The fill schema, refined.** `alreadyLabels` is `holdsLabels`; `multiply` keeps only `factor` (the UI names the presets); `trim_and_fix_case` gains `letterCase` (`keep`, `lower`, `upper`), since "fix case" did not say which; `convert` and `codeListId` are never set together; the stored shape is versioned snake_case (`version: 1`); a Combine expression names columns as `{column name}` placeholders, checked against the layout's columns and then by `assertSingleSqlExpression`.
- **One bad value never breaks the combined dataset.** Every fill is cast with `TRY_CAST`, dates parse with `TRY_STRPTIME`, and `pad_text` pads only digit strings shorter than the length (DuckDB's `lpad` truncates longer ones). A combined dataset over 100 sources would otherwise fail every query for one unparseable date. The pane's example and the preview show what becomes empty.
- **Each layout stacks its datasets with `SELECT *`.** Datasets of one layout share their column names ignoring case, so each layout's branch is `SELECT <fills> FROM (SELECT '<name>' AS "__ava_source_dataset", * FROM "<id>" UNION ALL BY NAME ...)`. Conversions are written once per layout, not once per dataset, and every output is aliased so `UNION ALL BY NAME` lines branches up.
- **Codes mode reconciles to the entry's primary list.** With **Codes**, every coded column outputs the codes of its entry's primary list; a layout using another coding translates through matching labels, and a pair with no counterpart in the primary list becomes empty rather than passing through as another list's code. A value that matches no pair of its list at all passes through as it is, as conversions keep unmatched values; in Codes mode over another coding, such a value can look like a primary code (known gap, listed in F136).
- **The combined dataset carries reference bindings for its coded columns.** `rpc_crosswalks__save_combined_dataset` writes them (the primary list, direction `encode` for labels and `decode` for codes), so the code-list tag, Ask Avandar's context, and the dictionary's Used by work with no new agent code. The crosswalk owns them and replaces them on every update, so **Apply a dictionary** is hidden on a combined dataset.
- **The browser compiles; the RPC stores.** The SQL and the output columns are built in TypeScript (as Data Explorer already saves virtual datasets), and the RPC reconciles the dataset's columns by name, keeping ids so descriptions and bindings survive an update. After an update the browser clears the dataset's cached rows and the virtual dataset query cache, since the loaded view is not keyed by the SQL.
- **A dataset whose columns changed since it was mapped is left out,** with a note in step 3, rather than failing the combined dataset on a missing column. Removing it and adding it back maps its new layout.
- **The reference layout changes only while no other layout is confirmed,** and changing it reseeds the columns of the combined dataset.
- **Matches are filled and confirmed at once; suggestions wait.** A score of 0.9 or more is filled as confirmed (solid line, "Name and type · 94%"); 0.6 to 0.9 is filled as a suggestion (dashed, Suggested, Accept or Reject). A layout is Mapped only after **Confirm and next**, which also confirms its suggestions and gives every unfilled column an explicit empty fill.
- **Step 3 counts datasets, not rows,** for unconfirmed mappings ("3 datasets have mappings you haven't confirmed."): counting rows would read every unconfirmed dataset before the user asked to.
- **Reference coverage is a percentage** of the other datasets' columns ("Matches 86% of the columns in the other datasets."), weighted by dataset count.
- **Only editors see crosswalks.** One permission, `data_sources__can_edit_crosswalks`, gates the Crosswalks group, **New crosswalk**, and the view. Viewers still read crosswalk rows under RLS, so Used by and the rail can name them; the rail's "Combined by" is plain text for them.
- **New crosswalk is its own toolbar button.** The toolbar has no Add menu (spec 7.1 assumed one): **New crosswalk** sits after **New dictionary**.
- **Saving happens on actions, not on a timer:** **Next**, every footer action, choosing another layout, changing steps, renaming, and step 3's create or update. Two editors saving one crosswalk at once: the last save wins (known gap).
- **A source's Refresh also clears the combined datasets that read it,** as it already does for linked datasets, since a virtual dataset's definition token does not follow its sources' rows.
- **Deleting a crosswalk keeps its combined dataset,** which stops updating; deleting the combined dataset leaves the crosswalk, whose step 3 offers **Create combined dataset** again.
- **The combined dataset's rail says "Combined by <crosswalk>".** The spec gave a combined dataset no way back to its crosswalk.
- **Export mapping writes one row per dataset and column,** in layout order then column position, so a layout family's mapping appears once per dataset it covers.

## Owner decisions on the open questions

Recommended by this plan, awaiting Juan Pablo's approval as a set. The tasks build the recommendations; a different answer changes the tasks named in the last column.

| # | Question | Recommendation | Where it lands |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | One PR or two? | Two. Part A (F136, Tasks 0 to 28) is everything spec 16 lists for slice 5 and is usable on its own; Part B (F137, Tasks 29 to 33) adds meaning suggestions, the long list, combining progress, and the measurement, frontend only. | Delivery; feature log |
| 2 | Who sees crosswalks? | Data Sources editors only, through one permission. Viewers see combined datasets as ordinary datasets, and "Combined by" as text. | Tasks 14, 16, 25 |
| 3 | When does the crosswalk save? | On **Next**, every footer action, choosing another layout, changing steps, renaming, and creating or updating the combined dataset. No timer. Last save wins between two editors (known gap). | Tasks 16, 17, 19, 22, 23 |
| 4 | Are high-confidence matches confirmed without a click? | Yes, 0.9 and up; 0.6 to 0.9 waits for Accept. A layout is Mapped only after **Confirm and next**. | Tasks 9, 15, 22 |
| 5 | What happens to a value that does not convert? | It becomes empty (`TRY_CAST`, `TRY_STRPTIME`), so one bad value never fails a combined dataset of 100 sources. The pane's example shows it first. | Tasks 10, 21 |
| 6 | In Codes mode, which codes come out? | The entry's primary list's codes. Another coding translates through matching labels; a value with no counterpart becomes empty. | Task 10 |
| 7 | Should the combined dataset carry bindings? | Yes: reference bindings on its coded columns, owned by the crosswalk, so the tag, Ask Avandar, and Used by work. **Apply a dictionary** is hidden on it. | Tasks 4, 12, 25 |
| 8 | How does Combine name columns? | `{column name}` placeholders, inserted from a menu and checked against the layout's columns, then `assertSingleSqlExpression`. | Tasks 7, 12, 21 |
| 9 | Can the reference layout change after mapping starts? | Only while no other layout is confirmed; changing it reseeds the columns. | Tasks 15, 17 |
| 10 | A dataset's columns changed after it was mapped? | Left out of the combined dataset, named in step 3; remove and re-add it to map the new layout. | Tasks 8, 12, 23 |
| 11 | Should a source's Refresh clear combined datasets that read it? | Yes, as for linked datasets. | Task 25 |
| 12 | Stale detection? | A fingerprint of each embedded list's pairs, not `updated_at`, which every dictionary save moves. | Tasks 1, 10, 25 |
| 13 | The source column's name? | Fixed as `source_dataset`; while it is added, no column of the combined dataset may use that name. | Tasks 3, 22, 23 |
| 14 | Deleting a crosswalk? | Keeps the combined dataset, which stops updating; the confirm says so. | Task 16 |
| 15 | A way back from the combined dataset to its crosswalk? | "Combined by <crosswalk>" in the rail. | Task 25 |
| 16 | Where does **New crosswalk** go? | A toolbar button after **New dictionary**; there is no Add menu. | Task 14 |
| 17 | Export mapping's shape? | One row per dataset and column: layout, dataset, output column, fill kind, source column, conversion, code list, status. In Part A. | Task 24 |
| 18 | Step 3's unconfirmed count? | Datasets, not rows. | Task 23 |
| 19 | Reference coverage copy? | A percentage of the other datasets' columns, weighted by dataset count. | Tasks 8, 17 |
| 20 | Meaning suggestions? | Reuse the dictionary-suggestions route's `matches` task (same consent, online and on device), with no server or prompt change, in Part B. | Task 29 |
| 21 | Open decision 4's rule? | Measure cold and warm first combines of 100 datasets in Part B; parallelize acquisition only past the threshold Task 32 records. | Task 32 |
